{"title":"ENVIRONMENT NOTES"}
</properties>
<iconMetadata>{"type":"emoji","emoji":"🚏"}</iconMetadata>
<content>
# ENVIRONMENT and DISASTER MANAGEMENT

🟢 Learn (asked in PYQs or in the water / coast / DM clusters) · 🟡 Answer-ready (not asked yet, but must be able to write on it: definition + 2 named examples + India's response + challenges + way forward) · ⚪ Skip (background, history)

<callout icon="🔑">
ENVIRONMENT (keywords to use : circular economy, Resource Decoupling, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), Cradle-to-Cradle, Common But Differentiated Responsibilities, Just Transition, Bioremediation: Using microorganisms to clean env, Keystone Species (species on which other depend), Blended Finance (PPP for green capital), Greenwashing, greenium, compensatory afforestation), Phytoremediation (t uses living green plants, to absorb, degrade, or stabilize toxic pollutants, environmental supplement plan ( undertake project to benefit environment because broke 2006 rules)
</callout>

<callout icon="💡" color="red_bg">
<toggle heading="h4">
🔑 PINCH-FC

- <b>P</b> Policy: weak laws, low penalties → better implementation + higher penalties + treat it as a prerequisite, not one more scheme
- <b>I</b> Innovation + Information: old tech, too little data (few monitors, weak forecasts) → new tech as the norm + sensors, satellites, real-time data
- <b>N</b> Nature: disasters, inversion, low wind make it worse → forecast-based action + nature-based fixes + plan by nature's units (basin, airshed, landscape)
- <b>C</b> Community (people at ground level): careless habits (littering, burning, overuse) + people left out or displaced → awareness, behaviour change, community-led action
- <b>H</b> Human activity + capacity: industry, vehicles, farms, power plants, cities + too few staff and facilities → clean the source + build capacity · rule: households and villagers = C, industry, cities and the state machine = H
- <b>F</b> Finance: polluting is cheaper, clean tech costs more → blended finance + greening of CSR + circular economy
- <b>C</b> Collaboration: pollution crosses borders, many agencies → Centre, states, industry and citizens act together
- <b>Effects</b>: Health · Environment · Economy · Governance · Society (poor, children, outdoor workers hit hardest)
- <b>Schemes</b> (same letters): P design flaw · I no outcome data · N ignores the basin, <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81dc-bf08-eb9ebd46d196/4251111b-206d-8135-bd44-001cec53684e">airshed o</span>r aquifer · C community left out · H no staff or capacity · F funds unspent or leaking · C no coordination
</toggle>
</callout>

<toggle heading="h1">
1\. CONSERVATION

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Biodiversity loss

- Frame: wildlife down 73% since 1970 (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4221111b-206d-81b3-be52-dd7820233080/4251111b-206d-813b-9049-001c946220cb">Living Planet Report) ·</span> India: 3,682 tigers (>70% of world), 22,446 elephants, but protected areas only 5.71% of land

<toggle>
Why India varies

- Latitude 8°–37°N (tropical Kerala → temperate J&K) + rainfall 100 mm → 11,000 mm (Cherrapunji); wet Western Ghats vs dry Deccan only ≈100 km apart
- Long coast, big rivers + cut-off islands → endemism (Andamans, Lakshadweep) + old Gondwana block → long time to evolve
- Northeast = meeting point of 3 realms (Indian, Indo-Malayan, Indo-Chinese)
- Hotspot criteria: at least 1,500 endemic vascular plants + lost at least 70% of original habitat
</toggle>

<toggle>
Carrying capacity

- The most individuals (or resource use) an area can support for ever without degrading its resources
- Exceeded → aquifers, rivers, grass run down + sudden population crash + overshoot lowers future capacity (an overfished lake never gets its fish back)
- In planning: carrying-capacity studies for hill towns (SC asked Himalayan states, 2023) + caps on tourists and vehicles + basis for EIA and master plans
- Failed: Joshimath sinking 2023 = capacity ignored
</toggle>

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>P</b>: laws diluted: jail → fines for minor offences
  <toggle>
  Jan Vishwas Act 2023

  - Amends 42 central laws (incl. EPA 1986, Air Act 1981): jail → penalties for minor offences, decide<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8149-83fa-faefe84288f9/4251111b-206d-81d2-a489-001ccf914d6c">d by adjudicating officers</span>
  - Fines go into an <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8199-806c-c33ec4c502e3/4251111b-206d-81b4-bfb2-001c5c905821">Environment Protection Fund (</span>EPA Section 15: ₹10,000 to ₹15 lakh)
  - Criticism: SC calls it "toothless" + harm continues (Futala Lake, illegal quarrying in Kerala forests) → fix: fines that deter + keep jail for serious harm
  </toggle>
- <b>I</b>: weak monitorin<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4221111b-206d-81a8-8bc5-fadced970615/4251111b-206d-811d-aa11-001c7047d453">g + many BMCs exist only on paper</span>
- <b>N</b>: invasive species (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4221111b-206d-814b-b417-e9545d4c4f84/4251111b-206d-81d7-a95d-001c20d2c879">Lantana)</span> + climate change (coral bleaching)
- <b>C</b>: poaching and wildlife trade (rhinos, pangolins worst hit, 2024; 100+ birds and turtles seized in Jalaun) + communities left out
- <b>H</b>: habitat lost to infrastructure and mining (≈77% of world's mines within 50 km of <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4221111b-206d-8161-ab65-cce9cf10cbd0/4251111b-206d-81ac-88bb-001c2a210d29">Key Biodiversity Areas)</span>
  <toggle>
  Great Nicobar

  - Transshipment port (Galathea Bay) + airport + 450 MW power plant + township, near the Malacca, Sunda, Lombok straits → cargo + defence
  - Concerns: Shompen (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81aa-9803-e6ff4d93acd2/4251111b-206d-819c-942d-001c44d28550">PVTG) a</span>nd Nicobarese displaced + leatherback turtle nesting + ≈9.6 lakh trees cut + mangroves lost + sits on the 2004 tsunam<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81aa-9803-e6ff4d93acd2/4251111b-206d-8109-99b4-001ca98a5702">i megathrust</span>
  - Forest rights not settled under FRA (A&N says its 1956 Aboriginal Tribes law, under which the administration alone can divert land, is enough; FRA needs Gram Sabha consent) · NGT 2023 upheld clearances → committee cleared the port again (Feb 2026)
  - Way forward: phased, ecologically sensitive, community-inclusive
  </toggle>
- <b>F</b>: finance gap (≈\$700 billion a year worldwide; India's NBSAP needs ₹81,664 crore a year)
- <b>C</b>: Centre–state fights (Kerala wants power to declare "<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4221111b-206d-81b6-a5c9-cdbd6d669759/4251111b-206d-81f0-965c-001cf70ef786">vermin"</span>)

<b>Effects</b>

- Environment: lost pollination, clean water, carbon storage · Economy: forests support ≈275 million livelihoods · Health<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81af-8613-d36c42b600f1/4251111b-206d-810c-b711-001ca0bc37ee">: zoonoses</span> (Nipah)
- Society: human–wildlife conflict
  <toggle>
  Human–wildlife conflict

  - 1,630 people killed by animals (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81c4-bb44-c7c50215768c/4251111b-206d-8114-b0cb-001cdc610cdf">ADSI 2024) + Kerala declared i</span>t a state-specific disaster + elephant conflict rising (Jharkhand, West Bengal) + crop loss, retaliatory killing
  - Why: more animals, same 5% protected-area network → they spill into farms and towns (langurs misused in Gurugram)
  - Fix: National HWC Mitigation Strateg<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81d6-b742-f8cdc9ab46b4/4251111b-206d-8174-88e3-001c41a70279">y 2021–26 + SOPs (tiger</span>, leopard, elephant) + early warnings (SMS, sensors, GPS collars) + bee-hive and solar fences + crops elephants avoid (chilli, citrus, ginger)
  - SC: ₹10 lakh for each human death + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81db-b924-cab8f666bf0b/4251111b-206d-8160-b107-001ce969fd38">landscape approach + c</span>orridors
  </toggle>

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>P</b>: strong laws
  <toggle>
  WPA 1972

  - 2022 amendment: 6 schedules → 4 (I highest protection, II high, III plants, IV CITES species)
  - Protected areas: National Parks (no human use) → Sanctuaries (some rights) → Conservation Reserves (buffers, corridors) → Community Reserves (local land)
  - Bodies: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81a7-83e7-df94a74b9237/4251111b-206d-81c1-8e76-001c530c4b6b">NBWL (PM chairs)</span> + NTCA (tigers) + WCCB (wildlife crime) + CZA (zoos)
  - Base: Art 48A (DPSP) + Art 51A(g) + forests and wild animals on the Concurrent List (42nd Amendment, 1976)
  - Worked: Kaziranga (zero rhino poaching 2022<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8173-82c4-edaf49daa399/4251111b-206d-8121-8899-001cd3689da6">) + TX2 met</span> in 2018 · Failed: Great Indian Bustard (Schedule I since 1972, ≈130 left)
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  BD Act 2002

  - Regulates access to biological resources, stop<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8133-9803-eae90e59a936/4251111b-206d-8159-a9d2-001cc2b03319">s biopiracy</span>, shares benefits · 3 tiers: NBA → State Biodiversity Boards → BMCs (1.4 lakh, keep People's Biodiversity Registers)
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81a2-afc7-cdc95ee9c6ef/4251111b-206d-8107-ac0f-001cd172a8d0">Biodiversity Heritage Sites (</span>Kaya Kalp Vriksh, Punjab; Arittapatti, Madurai → tungsten mine cancelled 2025)
  - 2023 amendment + 2025 rules: jail → fines + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81d7-99b6-d54fdcabad56/4251111b-206d-81ae-a502-001c6d83cc59">AYUSH exempt</span> + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81d7-99b6-d54fdcabad56/4251111b-206d-81aa-ad26-001cde8d45c7">digital sequence data covered</span> + benefit share 0.2–0.6% (5%+ high value), 60–75% to local communities
  - Worked: Kani tribe, Kerala (Jeevani drug, royalty shared) · Failed: Bt brinjal biopiracy case (2011, dragged for years)
  - Traditional knowledge: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-815e-9c92-f755256ed948/4251111b-206d-811a-88be-001cd99df592">TKDL +</span> <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-815e-9c92-f755256ed948/4251111b-206d-8105-a88a-001c152a842b">PPVFR Act 2001 + GI Act 1999 →</span> problems: biopiracy, poor records → pay TK holders + benefit sharin<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-815e-9c92-f755256ed948/4251111b-206d-81ba-8efe-001c111e256f">g under Nagoya</span>
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  Eco-sensitive zones

  - Buffers around protected areas under EPA 1986: prohibited (mining, polluting industry) / regulated (tree felling, hotels) / permitted (local farming)
  - Worke<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81f1-b558-f2433af40e62/4251111b-206d-8142-a75b-001c57405581">d: Mahabaleshwar</span>–Panchgani (2001) · Mixed: SC's 1-km ESZ round every PA (2022) relaxed in 2023 · Failed: Netala bypass, Bhagirathi ESZ (2025)
  </toggle>
- <b>I</b><span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-819a-97ec-ceb190a32c7b/4251111b-206d-81ab-ad7a-001cb14754d2">: DNA lab at WII</span> + drones + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-819a-97ec-ceb190a32c7b/4251111b-206d-81f7-908a-001c8916dc73">eco-bridges</span> (1.4 km underpass on the MP–Maharashtra border)
- <b>N</b>: species recovery: Project Tiger (1973), Elephant (1992), Cheetah (2022, many deaths) + corridors beyond the 5% PAs + landscape approach (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8125-ac42-e548fe8824f9/4251111b-206d-813f-9e86-001c6ab4680b">NWAP,</span> but non-binding)
- <b>C</b>: communities as guardians: 1.4 lakh BMCs + People's Biodiversity Registers
  <toggle>
  People's movements

  - Chipko (1973, Uttarakhand): non-violent hugging of trees → commercial logging banned in the Himalaya
  - Appiko (1983, Karnataka) + Silent Valley (1984: dam dropped → National Park) + Anti-Tehri Dam + Narmada Bachao Andolan (1985–)
  - NGOs and rehabilitation PYQs (2024, 2016) → see EIA
  </toggle>
- <b>F</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-819f-b4cb-d35ffe43c0c1/4251111b-206d-81a3-b24e-001caf2e6796">BIOFIN + CSR money +</span> Cali Fund + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-819f-b4cb-d35ffe43c0c1/4251111b-206d-816f-b0b9-001caa05ad9e">BRSR (top 1,000</span> listed firms report their environmental impact)
- <b>C</b>: global deals + IBCA (India-led big-cat alliance, 2023)
  <toggle>
  <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-817e-b941-db1e2629f467/4251111b-206d-8100-85fc-001c1f248a1c">KMGBF + C</span>OP16

  - KMGBF (CBD COP15, 2022): 23 targets by 2030: protect 30% of land and sea <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8148-845d-df0907ec84bb/4251111b-206d-81b0-b73a-001cfbc54d39">(30x30)</span> + restore 30% + halve invasive species + cut \$500 billion harmful subsidies + raise \$200 billion a year
  - Replaced the <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8167-bdb3-f253433c0c49/4251111b-206d-8117-8578-001c10b9fcec">Aichi targets (</span>none of 20 fully met by 2020) · <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8167-bdb3-f253433c0c49/4251111b-206d-8159-b14e-001c56e20868">Protected Planet 2024</span>: 17.6% land, 8.4% ocean protected
  - COP16, Cali (2024): Cali Fund (companies using digital sequence data pay 1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue, voluntary) + permanent body for Indigenous peoples · ran out of quorum, resumed in Rome 2025
  - Gaps: Cali Fund voluntary (first private payment only Nov 2025) + ≈700 billion dollars a year finance gap → fix: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8128-bbdd-d331ace083b5/4251111b-206d-81ac-9f78-001c1f84e75a">binding DSI payments + Kunming Biodiversity Fund</span>
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  NBSAP + national report

  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-810b-b87a-fb5f50de9b23/4251111b-206d-8136-8e7f-001c1306e60a">NBSAP 2024–30: 23</span> national targets matched to KMGBF + whole-of-government (23 ministries) + whole-of-society · released at Cali, one of 44 countries on time
  - Runs through NBA → SBB → BMC + BIOFIN (₹81,664 crore a year needed)
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8186-94d1-cc4faffad1e0/4251111b-206d-81d8-9cc4-001c5fffbf0d">7th national report t</span>o the CBD: forest + tree cover 25.1% + 24.1 million ha restored (Bonn pledge 26) + 100 Ramsar sites + first counts of snow leopards (718) and river dolphins (6,327)
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  Other conventions

  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81d3-9fd3-de1bcce90cd8/4251111b-206d-812a-8f0d-001c1abafc76">CITES (1973)</span>: controls trade in endangered species (India got star tortoise, otter into Appendix I, 2019)
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81eb-a923-f29a6368613d/4251111b-206d-8120-9898-001c1aa31346">CMS (1979):</span> migratory species (India hosted COP13, Gandhinagar 2020; GIB added) + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81eb-a923-f29a6368613d/4251111b-206d-81bc-8a46-001cdc1fba72">MAB (1971)</span>: 18 biosphere reserves
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81bb-a8d3-e32af6c0d313/4251111b-206d-8172-b4de-001cba247cbc">ITPGRFA (2001)</span>: shares 64 crops (≈80% of plant diet) · India guards sovereign rights + digital sequence data = digital biopiracy risk
  - Gaps: weak enforcement (illegal wildlife trade) + targets not binding (Aichi missed) → fix: WPA Schedule IV mirrors CITES + finance for the South
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  High Seas Treaty

  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-819f-9065-f19d3eea4899/4251111b-206d-81ec-bdbf-001c07735c44">BBNJ:</span> share benefits from high-seas genetic finds + high-seas marine protected areas + EIA for high-seas projects + help for developing countries
  - In force Jan 2026 after 60 ratifications; first COP Jan 2027 · India signed (Sep 2024), needs a domestic law to ratify
  - Issues: not universal + no punishing body + weak technology transfer → fix: ratify + build deep-sea research capacity
  </toggle>
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Forests

- Frame: forest 21% of area + forest and tree cover 25.17% (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4221111b-206d-8134-93c0-fb8278c9cedd/4251111b-206d-81fc-aeb4-001c79c8e5f0">ISFR 2023)</span> + 9th in forest area, 3rd in net gain (FAO 2025) + supports ≈275 million livelihoods

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>P</b>: laws diluted (2023 amendment narrowed "forest" → ≈28% of actual forest, unrecorded, loses cover)
- <b>N</b>: warming → more forest fires (36% of forest cover fire-prone)
- <b>C</b>: encroachment (10,000+ acres of Odisha's reserved forests) + field-burning fires + Gram Sabhas bypassed in diversions (MP, Odisha)
- <b>H</b>: diversion for mining (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4221111b-206d-814f-acce-d4720baede05/4251111b-206d-81e9-ab4e-001cbf208586">Hasdeo Arand)</span> + plantations (oil palm in the NE) + 3.3% lost 2001–2022
- <b>F</b>: forest finance gap \$216 billion to 2030 (UNEP)

<b>Effects</b>

- Environment: forest carbon stock ≈7,285 million t (55% in soil) + shield against storms and floods · Economy: timber, minor forest produce, ≈275 million livelihoods · Society: tribals lose land and forest rights

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>P</b>: forest laws
  <toggle>
  Indian Forest Act 1927

  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-813e-8998-cdb74e7f1417/4251111b-206d-81ce-986d-001c78cbca57">Colonial law for timber revenue</span>: Reserved, Protected, Village, Private forests + punishes unauthorised use
  - Worked: 2017 amendment (bamboo outside forests freed from transit permits) · Failed: 2019 draft (arms for forest officers) withdrawn after tribal protests
  - Fix: align with FRA (Gram Sabha say) + digitise records
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  FCA 1980 + CAMPA

  - Centre must approve diverting forest land + compensatory afforestation (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81fc-aa9b-c5008f1b6beb/4251111b-206d-81ee-93e4-001cdbc9a659">CA) for every diversion</span>
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8192-a047-c135778f541d/4251111b-206d-81cb-a9ba-001ca4703b42">Godavarman (1996)</span>: "forest" = dictionary meaning → FCA covers all forests, recorded or not
  - Failed: Kancha Gachibowli, Hyderabad (2025): urban project vs green <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8100-9ffa-c4d237b402d2/4251111b-206d-8119-b847-001c5d512926">lung near KBR</span> National Park → SC put ecology over convenience
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-811d-aa09-f3d34147cc26/4251111b-206d-8148-992e-001c5ed7bef8">CAF Act 2016 (CAMPA</span> funds): 85% of CA target met (2019–24) · problems: poor sapling survival, late plans, misuse → geo-tag CA site<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-811d-aa09-f3d34147cc26/4251111b-206d-8183-a37e-001c2cc01b01">s (e-Green Watch</span>, PARIVESH 2.0)
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  2023 amendment + 2025 rules

  - Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam: only forest recorded on/after 25 Oct 1980 protected → ≈28% of actual forest (unrecorded) loses cover + exempts land within 100 km of borders for strategic projects + zoos, safaris = "forestry"
  - SC interim order (Feb 2024): keep the dictionary meaning ti<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8107-b118-e13672c9c1ce/4251111b-206d-8195-9e10-001c2ea188d6">ll deemed-forest records</span> are ready
  - 2025 rules: work can start <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8157-ba7b-dd738d52b055/4251111b-206d-8196-85c1-001ca5875dc7">after Stage-I +</span> critical-mineral mines exempt from public hearing + CA land need not be notified Protected Forest
  - Border exemption: a 100 km line swallows almost all of the NE, high Himalaya and A&N → hotspots open to projects without EIA
  - Fix: notify CA land as Protected Forest + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-814c-abc7-f431eb47f053/4251111b-206d-812f-b6ae-001cc3ea590b">all approvals on PARIVESH + no net loss</span> of forest (as SC asked)
  </toggle>
- <b>I</b>: geo-tagging + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8162-a3fd-c351d923707b/4251111b-206d-8155-b545-001c7b82d347">FSI fire alerts</span> + digital forest records
- <b>N</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8103-89c1-c80a618a4833/4251111b-206d-81d6-a281-001cea1ce23e">Green India Mission (+5</span> million ha) + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8103-89c1-c80a618a4833/4251111b-206d-8196-b872-001c11a692b0">Bonn Challenge (24</span>.1 of 26 million ha done) + native species with survival audits (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8103-89c1-c80a618a4833/4251111b-206d-8114-8364-001c3b74d804">Miyawaki</span>)
- <b>C</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-815a-8c05-fab9f9655288/4251111b-206d-81d9-987c-001cc6089f0d">Joint Forest Management (</span>Sukhomajri model) + forest rights
  <toggle>
  FRA 2006

  - Restores individual and community forest rights of tribals and forest dwellers; Gram Sabha manages and conserves; overrides the 1927 Act
  - Worked: Mendha Lekha (first <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8104-9f6e-f58679c8a3ec/4251111b-206d-81c9-bc9b-001c877f8ed6">community forest rights, 1,800</span> ha, zero deforestation) + Niyamgiri 2013 (all 12 Gram Sabhas rejected Vedanta)
  - Gaps: community claims pending in 65% of eligible villages (2025) + Gram Sabhas bypassed (Assam oil palm) + SC eviction order 2019 (stayed)
  - Step: FRA cells in tribal districts to clear <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8162-bab8-d8ed5c8ee116/4251111b-206d-8141-b509-001c600bb26d">pending claims (Dharti Aaba</span> Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, 2024)
  - Fix: time-bound claims + legal literacy + Gram Sabha consent before any diversion
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  Sacred groves

  - Community-protected forest patches (Khasi, Garo hills; 1,200+ mapped by Kerala, 2025)
  - MoEFCC (2025) considering them as community reserves under WPA + nominated to UNESCO as a traditional conservation landscape (2025) + Tribal Ministry wants them counted in India's carbon-sink goal (NDC)
  </toggle>
- <b>F</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81d1-94e1-d25c468c5832/4251111b-206d-81e6-99ff-001ce84b703d">REDD+ p</span>ayments for standing forests + Japan's Forest Environment Tax
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Fragile ecosystems

- Frame: carbon stores + storm shields + biodiversity hubs: wetlands 6% of land but 40% of species · mangroves store 3x the carbon of forests · corals hold 25% of marine species · peat holds 5x forest carbon per sq m

<b>Threats</b>

- <b>P</b>: protection stuck (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81e1-8172-feb7ed7a7989/4251111b-206d-812c-ab16-001c4ebdc0d9">Western Ghats ESA draft</span> reissued 6 times since 2014)
- <b>N</b>: warming → bleaching, sea-level rise, algal blooms + invasive species (water hyacinth)
- <b>C</b>: encroachment (India lost 2 of every 5 wetlands in 30 years) + plastic and sewage
- <b>H</b>: shrimp farms, reclamation (Mumbai's mangroves), quarrying, coastal building
- <b>F</b>: their services are unpriced, so they look like "wasteland"

<b>Fixes</b>

- <b>P</b>: notify and enforce (Wetland Rules 2017, <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8184-aaa6-df60c61bacd7/4251111b-206d-8148-bc0c-001cf2e992ea">CRZ, ESA</span>)
- <b>I</b>: map and <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81c6-a19e-d939bdb391bc/4251111b-206d-8102-bd02-001c39f8837c">monitor (INCOIS Coastal Vulnerability</span> Index + digital wetland inventories)
- <b>N</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8187-9bb9-e8d1214a2efd/4251111b-206d-81dd-8af8-001c28c166bf">restore (MISHTI</span>, artificial reefs) + keep them as bio-shields in coastal plans
- <b>C</b>: community-led use (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81b6-ab4c-f2d46ae8ce20/4251111b-206d-8182-89ce-001cfe58aa6c">Mission Sahbhagita,</span> SAIME)
- <b>F</b>: blue carbon credits to pay for protection

<b>Ecosystems</b>

- Wetlands
  <toggle>
  Wetlands

  - India: ≈7 lakh wetlands, 16 million ha (4.86% of area) + lost 2 of every 5 in 30 years · J&K: 74% of lakes vanished or shrank since 1967 (CAG)
  - Ramsar Convention (1971, Ramsar, Iran; India joined 1982): 100 sites (oldest Chilika, Keoladeo 1981; most in Tamil Nadu) + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-814f-b4c6-de2da164bfdf/4251111b-206d-8120-92c8-001c229f96e7">Montreux Record o</span>f threatened sites (Loktak, Keoladeo) + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-814f-b4c6-de2da164bfdf/4251111b-206d-815a-9f67-001c940140e3">Wetland Cities</span> (Indore, Udaipur)
  - Wise use = keep a wetland's ecological character while people use it (national plans + laws + management + public education)
  - National Wetland Conservation Programme (1985–86) → merged with lake plan into <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8165-8f71-e5c691699614/4251111b-206d-81f2-b158-001cbd75d625">NPCA (2013) + W</span>etland Rules 2017 (State Wetland Authorities, inventories, no reclamation) + Wetland Wise Use framework 2024 + Mission Sahbhagita
  - India at Ramsar COP15 (2025): "Sustainable Lifestyles for Wetlands" resolution (linked to LiFE), backed by 172 countries
  </toggle>
- Mangroves
  <toggle>
  Mangroves

  - Salt-tolerant trees of the tide zone: 0.15% of India's area · 3x forest carbon (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8106-94e9-cff6fb4968f2/4251111b-206d-81e8-9cc2-001c55bf643b">blue carbon)</span> + cut flood depth 15–20%
  - Worked: Sundarbans during Amphan 2020 (bio-shield) · Failed: Mumbai lost mangroves to reclamation → Bombay HC (2018) made all mangroves protected forest
  - Threats: shrimp farms + coastal building + oil spills, plastic + sea-level rise → half the world's mangroves at risk
  - India: MISHTI (2023) + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-818d-bd4d-e2e6e2cb118d/4251111b-206d-8170-835f-001c66893666">SAIME (shrimp</span> farming inside mangroves, Sundarbans pilot) → fix: shrimp farms outside mangroves + blue carbon credits
  </toggle>
- Coral reefs
  <toggle>
  Coral bleaching

  - Corals live with algae (zooxanthellae) that feed them → heat stress → coral expels the algae → turns white · needs clean water + 23–29°C
  - India: Gulf of Kachchh + Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay + Lakshadweep + Andaman & Nicobar
  - Failed: Lakshadweep hit by the 4th global bleaching (2024) · Worked: Vaan island artificial reefs slowed erosion
  - India: WPA Schedule I + ban on coral and <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-811a-9ce0-fd4003db091f/4251111b-206d-8199-b714-001c991a8eb7">sand in construction + ICRI member</span> → fix: cut runoff + coral cryobank <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-811a-9ce0-fd4003db091f/4251111b-206d-81a5-a396-001ca858d3a1">+ Biorock</span> (Gulf of Kutch)
  </toggle>
- Western Ghats
  <toggle>
  Western Ghats

  - Biodiversity hotspot (endemics: Nilgiri tahr) + UNESCO site (2012) + water tower of the south (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri)
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8182-bcce-f841868007f7/4251111b-206d-81f4-bf18-001ccd637e84">Gadgil Committee (2011)</span> vs Kasturirangan (2013: 37% as ESA) → Karnataka rejected → ESA draft reissued 6 times, still not final
  - Failed: Wayanad 2024 (quarrying in the Gadgil-flagged zone) · Worked: Silent Valley 1984
  - Fix: finalise the ESA with states on board + no quarrying on steep slopes <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8196-b64d-fcc34fdba8e5/4251111b-206d-8123-bd5d-001cfd72f106">+ Western Ghats Ecology Authority</span>
  </toggle>
- Peatlands + marine protected areas
  <toggle>
  Peatlands + MPAs

  - Peat = plant matter that hasn't rotted for centuries (no oxygen) → 5x forest carbon per sq m; drained peat burns (Indonesia fires) → UNEP Global Peatlands Initiative (UNFCCC COP22, Marrakech)
  - Marine protected areas: Gulf of Mannar marine park, Gahirmatha (Odisha), Lothian island (WB)
  </toggle>
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Mining

- Frame: minerals drive the economy, but ≈77% of the world's mines sit within 50 km of Key Biodiversity Areas · sand is the 2nd most used resource after water; India's gap ≈300 million t a year

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>P</b>: sand is a "<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8132-bc95-c7e51fc06009/4251111b-206d-818d-af65-001cbe63cc51">minor mineral"</span> (MMDR Act 1957) → states regulate loosely + Go/No-Go diluted
- <b>I</b>: illegal mining hard to track (Goa, Bellary iron ore)
- <b>C</b>: sand mafia: low entry barrier, high profits
- <b>H</b>: urbanisation → demand for concrete and minerals
- <b>F</b>: mineral revenue vs ecology
- <b>C</b>: each state its own definition and rules (Aravallis)

<b>Effects</b>

- Forest and land lost + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81a0-b20f-df6a1ea58c4d/4251111b-206d-817b-9aaf-001c4c8297a5">acid mine drainage,</span> heavy metals in water + groundwater falls + dust → lung disease + subsidence and underground fires (Jharia) + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81a0-b20f-df6a1ea58c4d/4251111b-206d-8101-a659-001ca66c014f">tailings dams b</span>urst + tribals displaced
- Cases: Goa and Bellary iron ore (illegal mining, SC bans) + Jharia coal fires

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>P</b><span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81db-a372-e777153219d1/4251111b-206d-8188-a4d3-001ce1cf07ba">: EIA + District Survey Reports</span> + Sustainable Sand Mining Guidelines 2016 + Enforcement Guidelines 2020 (mine only what rivers refill) + Deepak Kumar case (2012: clearance even for small sand mines)
  <toggle>
  Go / No-Go zones

  - MoEF + Coal Ministry (2009–10): coal blocks split into "Go" (mining allowed) and "No-Go" (dense forest: >30% gross or >10% <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81f4-af21-e4290e437458/4251111b-206d-81b7-8d4a-001cf7cf0ab0">weighted forest cover) → a</span>bout a third No-Go → later diluted ("<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81f4-af21-e4290e437458/4251111b-206d-816e-9fe3-001c29e7d68c">inviolate forest")</span>
  - Revived: SC in <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8131-94fa-efd6a46c5005/4251111b-206d-81c8-a129-001c21a599ac">Saranda (2025) o</span>rdered a mining plan with Go/No-Go zones from geo-referenced ecological maps → same model asked for the Aravallis
  </toggle>
- <b>I</b>: drones (Telangana; Punjab with IIT Ropar) + GPS-tracked trucks + digital sand tracking + satellite checks
- <b>N</b>: mine closure plans + reclaim and afforest mined land
- <b>C</b>: Punjab model: farmers legally mine up to 3 ft on their land + registered crusher sites → starves illegal cartels
- <b>H</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81db-983b-c02e5ebe3733/4251111b-206d-8130-9fab-001cb244f832">M-Sand (</span>crushed rock) + recycle construction waste
- <b>F</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8157-88e4-e35eb60e3bcc/4251111b-206d-8102-b4a8-001cbe7f6015">DMF/PMKKKY</span> money for affected people + star rating of mines

<b>Cases</b>

- Aravallis
  <toggle>
  Aravallis

  - Oldest fold mountains (≈692 km, Delhi → Haryana → Rajasthan → Gujarat): wall against the Thar + groundwater + Khetri copper
  - Definition row: SC (Nov 2025) accepted "hill = 100 m above surroundings, range = 2+ hills within 500 m" → low hills lose protection → protests → SC stayed it (Dec 2025) + Centre banned new leases (except critical minerals)
  - Fix: one continuous ridge, one definition + Aravalli Green Wall (5 km buffer, 4 states) + Go/No-Go mining plan
  - Worked: Save Aravalli movement (Rajendra Singh → SC halted Sariska mining, 1990) + Mangar Bani no-construction zone
  </toggle>
- Sand mining
  <toggle>
  River sand mining

  - Riverbed mining changes river flow + lowers groundwater + kills river life + sand mafia violence
  - Fix: replenishment studies (SC) + M-Sand + drones + national aggregates body
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  Coastal sand mining + erosion

  - Coastal mining → beach and dune erosion + seawater into aquifers and farms + Olive Ridley nesting beaches lost (Odisha) + fish breeding grounds hit · Alappad, Kerala (mineral sand, "Save Alappad" 2019) · CRZ bans it
  - Coastal erosion: 33.6% of India's coast eroding (West Bengal 63%, Puducherry 57%, Kerala 45%) + coastline re-measured 7,500 → 11,098 km
  - Causes: sea-level rise + stronger cyclones + mangroves lost + sand mining, dredging + ports and seawalls <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8162-befe-d0bd3a647e2a/4251111b-206d-819c-8c51-001c29f227b0">block sand drift</span> + dams cut river silt
  - Fix: mangroves + sand nourishment + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81ed-9ed4-f716b426b066/4251111b-206d-815e-8248-001c295fbc19">Shoreline Management Plans +</span> CRZ 2019 <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81ed-9ed4-f716b426b066/4251111b-206d-81d7-bd96-001c3d30fb02">No Development Zones + W</span>orld Bank K-SHORE (Karnataka) + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81ed-9ed4-f716b426b066/4251111b-206d-8184-a49b-001cebd51a38">ICZMP (Odisha, West Bengal) + CMIS</span>
  </toggle>
</toggle>

<toggle>
OLD way

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Overview

<toggle color="gray">
PYQ 2019

- <b>2019 Q17 (15 marks):</b> Define the concept of carrying capacity of an ecosystem as relevant to an environment. Explain how understanding this concept is vital while planning for sustainable development of a region.
</toggle>

- 20% foresrts are under protection of state departments more than the Aichi target 11 (The Aichi Biodiversity Targets are a set of 20 global goals established in 2010 to combat the loss of biodiversity. They were part of the Strategic Plan for Biodiversity 2011–2020, adopted by the parties of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) during the COP10 summit in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan.) (target 11 : This is often considered the most famous Aichi Target. It aimed to protect: 17% of terrestrial and inland water areas 10% of coastal and marine area)
- Carrying capacity : the most individuals (or resource use) an area can support for ever without degrading its resources (Exceeded → resources run down (aquifers, rivers, grass) + sudden population crash + overshoot lowers the area's future capacity (overfished lake never gets its fish back even after fishing stops) + Used in planning: carrying-capacity studies for hill towns (SC asked Himalayan states for one, 2023) + caps on tourists and vehicles + basis for EIA and master plans (eg. Joshimath sinking 2023 = capacity ignored)
- <b>Examples</b>: Kaziranga, Assam (worked: one-horned rhino \~200 in 1905 → 2,600+ in 2022 via strict <span color="green_bg">protected area</span> + anti-poaching) + Great Indian Bustard, Rajasthan (failed: under 150 left, power-line collisions → SC 2021 ordered lines underground)
- <b>India's response</b>: PAs on 5.71% of land + Project Tiger / Elephant + <span color="green_bg">NBSAP 2024–30</span> + Biological Diversity Act + carrying-capacity studies for hill towns
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Criteria for Biodiversity hotspots

<toggle color="gray">
PYQ 2018

- <b>2018 Q17 (15 marks):</b> How does biodiversity vary in India? How is the Biological Diversity Act,2002 helpful in conservation of flora and fauna?
</toggle>

<toggle>
<b>Why biodiversity varies across India</b>

Varies because: latitude 8°–37°N (tropical Kerala → temperate J&K) + rainfall 100 mm → 11,000 mm (Cherrapunji); wet Western Ghats vs dry Deccan rain shadow only \~100 km apart + 11,000 km coast and big rivers + islands cut off → endemism (Andamans, Lakshadweep) + old Gondwana block → long time to evolve + Northeast = meeting point of 3 realms (Indian, Indo-Malayan, Indo-Chinese)
</toggle>

- 1\. Species Richness: The region must have at least <span color="green_bg">1,500 species of vascular plants</span> as endemics.
- 2\. Threat Level: The region must have lost at least <span color="green_bg">70% of its original habitat</span>, indicating a high level of threat and a critical need for conservation attention
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Western Ghats

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: The Western Ghats, a key <span color="green_bg">biodiversity hotspot</span>
- <b>Significance</b>: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012) + source of Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri + brings monsoon rain to the peninsula (<span color="green_bg">water tower</span> of south India)
- <b>Examples</b>: Wayanad landslide, Jul 2024 (failed: villages in the Gadgil-flagged zone, quarrying + building on steep slopes) + Silent Valley, Kerala (1984, worked: people's campaign stopped a dam → National Park)
- <b>India's response</b>: Conservation efforts include ESA designations by the <span color="green_bg">Gadgil</span> (2011) and (increaising Economically sensitive area (ESA) designtion to 37% land) <span color="green_bg">Kasturirangan</span> (2013) Committees, community-led forest protection through JFM (joint forest management, and the Western Ghats Biosphere Reserve to balance ecological protection with sustainable development.
- <b>Challenges</b>: face threats from deforestation, mining, and infrastructure projects + Western Ghats <span color="green_bg">ESA</span> draft notification reissued 6 times since 2014, still not final (states object)
- <b>Way forward</b>: finalise the ESA notification with states on board + no quarrying or building on steep slopes + community-led protection (JFM, BMCs)
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 COP 16 UN Convention on Biological Diversity

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: Location: Cali, Colombia \| Theme: "Peace with Nature"
- <b>Pillars / key features</b>: Key Outcomes & Frameworks
  - The <span color="green_bg">Cali Fund</span> (DSI Mechanism): A landmark "benefit-sharing" agreement.
    - Requirement: Large companies (pharmaceutical, cosmetic, biotech) using <span color="green_bg">Digital Sequence Information</span> (DSI) from genetic resources must contribute to the fund.
  - Contribution: 1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue.
  - Beneficiaries: Funds are directed toward Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities (IPLCs) for biodiversity conservation.
  - Institutional Recognition: A new permanent subsidiary body was established to ensure the effective participation of Indigenous peoples in CBD processes.
  - Kunming Biodiversity Fund: Formally launched to support developing nations in hitting biodiversity targets.
  - Marine Conservation: Identification of "Ecologically or Biologically Significant Marine Areas" (EBSAs) to help achieve the <span color="green_bg">30-by-30</span> goal.
  - Technical Progress: Action plans were advanced regarding synthetic biology, management of invasive species, and the "One Health" approach (linking biodiversity to human health).
- <b>Examples</b>: Cali Fund (launched Feb 2025; first private payment only in Nov 2025, a small UK startup → voluntary model weak) + Protected Planet Report released at Cali (17.6% land, 8.4% ocean protected → far from <span color="green_bg">30x30</span>)
- <b>India's response</b>: released updated <span color="green_bg">NBSAP</span> at Cali (Oct 2024) → 23 national targets matched to KMGBF + <span color="green_bg">Whole of Government, Whole of Society</span> + asked for international finance to implement it → one of only 44 countries to submit by the end of COP16 (see 🟡 India – NBSAP 2024–30)
- <b>Challenges</b>: Cali Fund payments are voluntary + COP16 ran out of quorum on finance and had to resume in Rome (Feb 2025)
- <b>Way forward</b>: make DSI payments binding + close the <span color="green_bg">finance gap</span> + implement NBSAPs on time
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF)

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: Aims to halt biodiversity loss or reverse by 2030 (adopted at CBD COP15, Montreal, Dec 2022)
- <b>Pillars / key features</b>: 23 targets by 2030 like 30% land and sea conservation and halving invasive species + promote fair benefit-sharing (including via DSI)
- <b>Significance</b>: new global targets after the 2010 <span color="green_bg">Aichi targets</span> were missed (none of the 20 fully met by 2020)
- <b>Examples</b>: Protected Planet Report 2024 (failed so far: protection must double on land and triple at sea by 2030) + Salas y Gómez–Nazca ridges, SE Pacific (Chile-led, set to be among the first high-seas MPAs → helps Target 3)
- <b>India's response</b>: updated NBSAP (Oct 2024) maps India's 23 targets onto KMGBF's 23 + <span color="green_bg">30x30</span> via PAs, community reserves and OECMs + biodiversity finance via BIOFIN (see 🟡 India – NBSAP 2024–30)
- <b>Challenges</b>: close the \$700 billion finance gap
- <b>Way forward</b>: fund the targets (Cali Fund, Kunming Fund) + honest progress reports in each national report
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 India – NBSAP 2024–30

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: Alignment: Fully aligned with the <span color="green_bg">Kunming-Montreal</span> Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). + Core Objective: Halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030; "Living in Harmony with Nature" by 2050.
- <b>Pillars / key features</b>
  - Targets: 23 National Biodiversity Targets (NBTs) across three pillars: Threat Reduction, Sustainable Use, and Implementation Tools.
  - Approach: "Whole-of-Government" (23 ministries involved) and "Whole-of-Society" (incorporating Indigenous/local knowledge).
  - Finance: Supported by the Biodiversity Finance Initiative (BIOFIN); estimated annual requirement of ₹81,664 crore.
  - Mechanism: Three-tier governance (NBA → SBB → BMC) under the BD Act 2002 (amended 2023).
- <b>Significance (India's status)</b>
  - India recently submitted 7th national report under article 26 of convention on biological diversity
  - all 23 revised NBSAP indicators are on track and align with KMGBF
  - Forest + tree cover = 25.1 % of geographical area
  - Forest carbon stock reached 7,285.5 million tonnes (55% is soil organic carbon)
  - 24.1 million hectares (mha) restored or under restoration (<span color="green_bg">Bonn Challenge</span> pledge of 26 mha by 2030)
  - 100 <span color="green_bg">Ramsar</span> sites as of Jun 2026 (26 in 2014). (Ranks 1st in Asia and 3rd globally).
  - Wildlife Populations: 3,682 Tigers (>70% of global total), 22,446 Elephants, >4,000 Rhinos, and 891 Asiatic Lions.
    - First Assessments: Recorded 718 Snow Leopards and 6,327 Riverine Dolphins.
  - Protected Areas covers 5.71% of land area; marine protected areas have also increase
- <b>Examples</b>: Arittapatti, Madurai (worked: Tamil Nadu's first <span color="green_bg">Biodiversity Heritage Site</span>, 2022 → Centre cancelled a tungsten mining block there after protests, Jan 2025) + Project Cheetah, Kuno NP (2022, mixed: species recovery target, but many cheetah deaths in the first year)
- <b>India's response</b>: India implements by using PARVESH for green clearance, for eco sys restore (Bonn challenge (restore 26 million degraded land) , species recovery & genetic diversity (via species recovery program) + sustainable agriculture via natural and organic farming + Pollution reduction via national clean air programme + Urban ecosystem ( smart cities) + Access and benefit sharing via (Nagoya protocol mechanism) + Finance (CSR and Business responsibility and sustainability report (top 1000 firms) ) + capacity building via national one health mission
- <b>Challenges</b>: finance (₹81,664 crore a year needed) + many BMCs exist only on paper + species recovery mixed (cheetah deaths)
- <b>Way forward</b>: BIOFIN + CSR money for targets + empower <span color="green_bg">BMCs</span> and People's Biodiversity Registers + track all 23 targets in the 8th national report
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
⚪ Case study of eco-bridge a.k.a eco ducts

- Madhya Pradesh-Maharashtra Border Eco-Underpass: This eco-bridge will be one of India's longest underpasses, stretching across 1.4 kilometers. Situated on the Madhya Pradesh-Maharashtra border, the project is designed to support wildlife movement and enhance conservation efforts in the area
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 People’s movements

<toggle color="gray">
PYQ 2024, 2016

- <b>2024 Q8 (10 marks):</b> What role do environmental NGOs and activists play in influencing Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) outcomes for major projects in India? Cite four examples with all important details.
- <b>2016 Q14 (12.5 marks):</b> Rehabilitation of human settlements is one of the important environmental impacts which always attracts controversy while planning major projects. Discuss the measures suggested for mitigation of this impact while proposing major developmental projects.

- Inspired by it, the Appiko Movement (1983) in Karnataka promoted tree conservation through direct action.
