<toggle heading="h1">
5\. DISASTER MANAGEMENT

- (It is a planned, coordinated effort to reduce risk, build resilience, and protect lives and livelihoods.) (any disaster strategies : PARFREII (preparation thru monitoring (safe infra), awareness, risk assessment , finance, recovery, early warning, inter agency coordination, implementation via capacity building )

<toggle heading="h3">
DM CORE

<toggle heading="h4">
🔑 PARFREII

- <b>P</b> Preparation through monitoring (safe infrastructure)
- <b>A</b> Awareness
- <b>R</b> Risk assessment
- <b>F</b> Finance
- <b>R</b> Response + Recovery
- <b>E</b> Early warning
- <b>I</b> Inter-agency coordination
- <b>I</b> Implementation via capacity building
- Causes use PINCH-FC (top of Pollution) · Effects: Health · Environment · Economy · Governance · Society
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 DM spine

- Frame: India is multi-hazard: 59% of land quake-prone + 12% (40 million ha) flood-prone + 5,700 of 7,500 km coast exposed to cyclones and tsunamis + 68% of farmland drought-prone + 5.4 million displaced in 2024 (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4221111b-206d-81b8-a517-d14bb55c3d80/4251111b-206d-8105-9ad9-001cfe227332">IDMC)</span>

<toggle>
Risk formula

- Risk = Hazard × Vulnerability × Exposure (lower with more capacity) · hazard = event that can harm → disaster = when it overwhelms a community's capacity to cope
- Vulnerability, 4 types: physical (weak houses on slopes) + social (age, gender, caste, disability) + economic (poverty, no insurance) + environmental (degraded ecosystems)
- <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-818c-bdbb-e9ec4c411e61/4251111b-206d-8187-9943-001c40f729ae">Exposure: people and assets</span> in the hazard zone (Joshimath 2023: town on old landslide debris)
- <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81a5-8c23-ec86150d7712/4251111b-206d-815e-ae46-001c2d28f41f">Cascading risk</span>: one hazard sets off another (Chamoli 2021: rock-ice avalanche → flood → Tapovan tunnel · Sikkim 2023: GLOF → Chungthang dam breach)
</toggle>

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>P</b>: building codes poorly enforced + expert warnings ignored (Joshimath: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-816d-aa91-f1956533483a/4251111b-206d-81a8-8d87-001cf4e7d31a">Mishra Committee warned in 1976</span>)
- <b>I</b>: flash floods and cloudbursts hard to forecast, no local warning (Dharali, Uttarkashi 2025)
- <b>N</b>: the hazard itself + climate change makes extremes more frequent
- <b>C</b>: lakes and floodplains encroached (Chennai 2015) communities, and forest and tribals specially vulnerable (assam floods)
- <b>H</b>: building on unstable slopes + deforestation + mining + hydel projects (Himachal 2023)
- <b>F</b>: insurance covers only ≈3.7%, most losses uninsured
- <b>C</b>: agencies poorly coordinated (Kerala 2018 dam releases, Kedarnath 2013)

<b>Effects</b>

- Health: deaths and injuries · Environment: ecosystems wrecked · Economy: losses doubled in 20 years <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8122-bae7-d5542814496b/4251111b-206d-818f-b1b0-001c030836d2">(GAR 2025) ·</span> Governance: providing relief burden on states · Society: poor, women, disabled hit hardest

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>P</b>: retrofit schools and hospitals first + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8147-b911-df927cd26c4d/4251111b-206d-81e9-8e8f-001c9044c05c">safe infrastructure (CDRI)</span> · \$1 on DRR saves \$15 (GAR 2025)
- <b>A</b>: disaster lessons in NCERT Classes 8–10 + mock drills (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81d9-8450-e8c63152dce6/4251111b-206d-81df-a060-001ca57b4795">Exercise Suraksha Chakra 2025:</span> 55 sites, 18 districts in NCR)
- <b>R</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81c4-aa35-d99d11c971d9/4251111b-206d-8186-bbeb-001cdff5dee0">hazard maps + Disaster Risk Index</span> for sharing funds
- <b>F</b>: disaster funds + risk transfer
  <toggle>
  Disaster finance

  - 16th FC: ₹2.04 lakh crore for <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8170-80f9-d9268ca414b0/4251111b-206d-8112-869a-001c438c0109">SDRF + SDMF (</span>2026–31), up 27% + heatwaves and lightning added to notified disasters
  - SDRF 75:25 (90:10 Himalayan and NE) · <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8102-abab-cec60369cb83/4251111b-206d-81e0-b9a0-001cf1ac205d">NDRF 100% Centre</span>, for "severe" calamities · NDMF/SDMF for mitigation
  - Issues: one-size Disaster Risk Index misses hilly and coastal states + "severe" undefined + ₹4 lakh per death unchanged for a decade + index weights: hazard 70, vulnerability 30
  - Fix: blended finance <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8112-9504-fa87c87cf834/4251111b-206d-8164-99f3-001ca33fa994">+ debt-for-resilience swaps</span> + review the index every 5 years
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  Insurance

  - Only ≈1% protection; most disaster losses uninsured
  - Worked: Nagaland (2024), first state with <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8131-8a83-dba7d13221d0/4251111b-206d-8153-bb54-001c7fab5229">parametric insurance (</span>auto-payout when rain crosses a threshold) · Mixed<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8131-8a83-dba7d13221d0/4251111b-206d-8150-a2cf-001c2d009bca">: PMFBY</span> (late claims, states left in 2020)
  - India<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81ff-b3e1-e10194c5cd83/4251111b-206d-81ce-a901-001c5326f0f5">: Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act</span> (Dec 2025) + "Insurance for All by 2047" (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81ff-b3e1-e10194c5cd83/4251111b-206d-8182-a871-001c34e91eb1">IRDAI) +</span> GST on insurance cut to 0%
  </toggle>
- <b>R</b>: respons<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-811c-b54e-e5c670b4491f/4251111b-206d-8134-9f7b-001c3e4fbf32">e: NDRF (16 battalions)</span> + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-811c-b54e-e5c670b4491f/4251111b-206d-817e-8223-001c98dfa9d4">Incident Response System +</span> <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-811c-b54e-e5c670b4491f/4251111b-206d-81de-8c1b-001c842cb16e">ERSS-112 + golden hour (</span>Silkyara 2023: 41 rescued after 17 days) · recovery: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-811c-b54e-e5c670b4491f/4251111b-206d-81e2-b7a8-001c9490774f">post-disaster needs assessment +</span> <span color="green_bg">build back better</span> (Bhuj 2001: owner-driven rebuilding)
- <b>E</b>: early warning to the last mile (Pacific tsunami warning costs ≈4 million dollars a year vs ≈8 billion dollars of aid after 2004)
  <toggle>
  Early warning

  - SACHET (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8196-a446-da4091b8a6a0/4251111b-206d-81a0-83e2-001cc2d21b2f">Common Alerting Protocol)</span> + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8196-a446-da4091b8a6a0/4251111b-206d-811d-9a21-001c23966392">cell-broadcast alerts i</span>n local languages
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8127-9001-f4fbdf65cb0d/4251111b-206d-8199-a146-001cdad4be6d">Mission Mausam (</span>2024, ₹2,000 crore): 50 Doppler radars + AI forecasts · Bharat Forecast System: 6 km grid<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8127-9001-f4fbdf65cb0d/4251111b-206d-81e5-a39d-001c20fc96d2">, village-level nowcasts</span>
  - Worked: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81ce-8016-d7b0ac2e4384/4251111b-206d-8169-8ecf-001c5dd29d52">INCOIS tsunami centre</span> (alerts in minutes) · Failed: Dharali 2025 (no local warning)
  - UN Early Warnings for All by 2027
  </toggle>
- <b>I</b>: inter-agency coordination: National Executive Committee + Incident Response Teams + CDRI abroad
- <b>I</b>: capacity building<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8187-9221-fc4cbaa94ea2/4251111b-206d-81e5-a299-001c35133d17">: Aapda Mitra volunteers</span> + tech tools + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8187-9221-fc4cbaa94ea2/4251111b-206d-81a1-b375-001c2d170667">IUINDRR-NIDM network of 330+ universities</span>
  <toggle>
  New tech for DM

  - Risk tools<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81de-a220-e55b50a23eac/4251111b-206d-8178-a9a8-001c0c8b752d">: Web-DCRA</span>, Flood Hazard Atlas, Glacial Lake Dataset
  - Warnings: SACHET, Damini (lightning), Mausam app, NCRMP for coastal states + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-813f-a1b7-f4da8f8ee14d/4251111b-206d-8193-b8dd-001c56e818e3">Odisha's SATARK platform</span>
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8129-8cdc-c77144b0629b/4251111b-206d-81a8-a056-001c41fb5312">HADR abroad</span>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8129-8cdc-c77144b0629b/4251111b-206d-8156-bc1b-001c6e6da970">Operation Dost (</span>Türkiye, Syria) + Operation Brahma (Myanmar 2025)
  - Worked: Wayanad 2024 (Army built a 190-ft <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8109-a545-f3ce16472397/4251111b-206d-81f5-b39a-001c91532b3a">Bailey bridge in ≈</span>1.5 days)
  </toggle>
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 India's DM framework

- Frame: DM = planned, coordinated effort to reduce risk, build resilience and protect lives and livelihoods
- Shift: relief-centric → zero-casualty, proactive
  <toggle>
  Reactive → proactive

  - Relief after the event → risk reduction before it: DM Act 2005 covers the whole cycle
  - NDMP 2019 + DM Amendment Act 2025 + 16th FC disaster funds + Mission Mausam
  - Worked: Odisha, Phailin 2013 (≈10 lakh evacuated, ≈44 deaths vs ≈10,000 in the 1999 super cyclone)
  - Sendai + Paris + SDGs (all 2015) read together: NDMP aligns all three
  </toggle>
- The law
  <toggle>
  DM Act 2005

  - 3 tiers: NDMA (PM) → SDMA (CM) → DDMA (Collector) + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81cb-9d33-f447d4d8efe2/4251111b-206d-819d-8a35-001cf881ee95">National Executive Committee (Home Secretary)</span>
  - NDRF (force) + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8191-9205-d5a9fd216936/4251111b-206d-8137-bee2-001cd719bb75">NIDM (training)</span> + plans mandatory at every level + NDRF/SDRF funds
  - Used: COVID-19 lockdown (first nationwide use) · Failed: Uttarakhand 2013 (state authority had barely met)
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  DM Amendment Act 2025

  - Urban DM Authorities in every municipal corporation (except Delhi, Chandigarh), headed by the Commissioner
  - National and state disaster databases + NDMA sets minimum relief standards and audits plans + SDRF in every state
  - Gaps: NDMA still under MHA + member vacancies + vague urban plans
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  NDMP 2019

  - Aligns with Sendai, SDGs, Paris + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8118-8de9-c0292a07f47d/4251111b-206d-810a-9c5a-001c38a4445a">PM's 10-point agenda;</span> first plan 2016
  - Themes: understanding risk + inter-agency coordination + risk governance + capacity development + preparedness and response + recovery
  - Goals for 2022, 2027, 2030 + risk matrices for 20+ hazards + nodal ministry for each
  - Worked: Ahmedabad Heat Action Plan 2013 · Cyclone Fani 2019 (SOPs, NDRF pre-positioned)
  </toggle>
- Global frameworks
  <toggle>
  Sendai vs Hyogo

  - Sendai 2015–30, 7 targets: reduce deaths + people affected + economic loss + infrastructure damage · increase DRR strategies (by 2020) + international support + early warning access
  - 4 priorities: understand risk + strengthen risk governance + invest in DR<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81f4-8194-e35f65e64c3e/4251111b-206d-81d3-83bb-001c39b43e41">R + preparedness and build back better</span>
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8126-b3ee-efa63dca17a4/4251111b-206d-81a3-a976-001c3edf8af3">Hyogo 2005–15 (</span>5 priorities) managed disasters; Sendai manages risk: prevention over response + DRR in every sector + local ownership
  - India before Sendai: DM Act 2005, NDMA, NDRF · after: NDMP 2016/2019, 10-point agenda, CDRI 2019
  </toggle>

  <toggle>
  Resilience

  - Anticipate + absorb + adapt + recover, and "bounce forward" (build back better)
  - Measured by: early warning and risk info (anticipate) + strong infrastructure and safety nets (absorb) + flexible institutions (adapt) + fast, inclusive rebuilding (recover)
  - Worked: Odisha, Fani 2019 (≈12 lakh evacuated, ≈64 deaths) · Failed: Chennai 2015 (lakes built over)
  </toggle>
- Local level
  <toggle>
  Community DRR

  - National Project for Community-Based DRR in PRIs (₹507 crore, MoPR + NDMA): 20 states, 81 districts
  - Pozhuthana panchayat, Kerala 2018 (risk maps, village response teams) + Tampara wetland, Odisha (eco-DRR)
  - Aapda Mitra + SACHET alerts
  </toggle>

<b>Gaps</b>

- <b>P</b>: "severe calamity" undefined + sector laws scattered (EPA 1986, Factories Act 1948, <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8143-ae60-d9010e81a62d/4251111b-206d-8187-913c-001c39d1801c">Epidemic Diseases Act 1897</span>) + no fixed liability for officials
- <b>I</b>: disaster databases only from 2025
- <b>H</b>: member vacancies + many states still relief-heavy
- <b>F</b>: mitigation money under-used (CAG)

<b>Fixes</b>

- Enforce the 2025 amendments + DRR in every development plan + social audits of relief + regular Parliament review of NDMA + courts enforce duties (SC, Gaurav Kumar Bansal 2021: ex gratia for COVID deaths)
</toggle>
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h3">
HAZARDS

- <b>DM cycle</b>: before (prevention, mitigation → preparedness) → during (response) → after (recovery = rehabilitation + reconstruction) → build back better feeds the next round
- <b>NDMA's 6 pillars</b> (every hazard guideline): risk mapping · safe construction and retrofitting · regulation and enforcement · awareness and preparedness (early warning) · capacity building · response. Each NDMA toggle below adds only that hazard's extras

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Earthquakes

- Frame: 59% of land in Zones II–V <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81cc-82aa-dd5572e5edf5/4251111b-206d-81bf-b50a-001c295d48f3">(IS 1893:2016)</span> · BIS 2025 code added Zone VI, withdrawn Mar 2026 → 2016 code back

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>P</b>: building codes not enforced + most houses non-engineered
- <b>I</b>: earthquake early warning only a pilot (Uttarakhand)
- <b>N</b>: Indian plate pushing into Eurasia (Himalaya, NE) + intraplate stress (Latur 1993)
- <b>C</b>: low awareness, little drill culture
- <b>H</b>: dense cities on soft soil + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8198-8ce5-cb7a4becbc8d/4251111b-206d-810e-a743-001c2100292c">reservoir-induced quakes</span> (dams, mining)

<b>Effects</b>: buildings kill, not the shaking + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-816d-87b8-f0ba32f473c5/4251111b-206d-81f4-829f-001cff067805">liquefaction,</span> landslides, tsunamis + roads, power, hospitals cut

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>NDMA guideline</b>
  <toggle>
  NDMA Earthquakes

  - Earthquake-resistant new construction + selective retrofitting of schools and hospitals
  - Enforce codes (IS 1893, National Building Code) + Incident Command System and Emergency Operations Centres
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8153-9d59-c3b78ed07e38/4251111b-206d-8107-9306-001ce809d5da">National Earthquake Risk Mitigation Project +</span> National Centre for Seismology
  </toggle>
- <b>P</b>: retrofit schools and hospitals first
- <b>A</b>: drills (Exercise Suraksha Chakra 2025, NCR)
- <b>R</b>: Earthquake Disaster Risk Index for 50 cities
- <b>E</b>: seismic observatories 80 (2014) → 168 (2025) + BhooKamp and India Quake apps
- <b>I</b>: NDRF: 16 battalions, 1,149 personnel each
- Cases
  <toggle>
  Major earthquakes

  - Latur 1993 (≈10,000 dead, on the "stable" Deccan plate)
  - Bhuj 2001 (M7.7, ≈20,000 dead) → Gujarat rebuilt wit<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81bc-a09e-f1452c59d1a1/4251111b-206d-8154-831a-001cdce005a4">h GSDMA</span> + owner-driven reconstruction (worked)
  - Kashmir 2005 (M7.6) · Sikkim 2011 (M6.9) · Nepal 2015 (M7.8, Bihar hit) · Imphal 2016 (M6.7)
  - World: Pacific Ring of Fire (≈90% of earthquakes, ≈75% of active volcanoes) → Kamchatka M8.8 (2025) sent tsunami waves to Russia and Japan
  </toggle>
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Tsunamis

- Frame: 13 tsunamis in the Indian Ocean in 300 years; 2004 the most destructive to hit India

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>N</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81a6-9de2-c314933f9173/4251111b-206d-8183-9139-001c6334c202">undersea megathrust quakes</span> (2004: M9.1 Sumatra–Andaman, Indian plate under Burma plate) + submarine landslides, volcanic collapse
- <b>H</b>: building in coastal no-development zones + mangroves cleared

<b>Effects</b>: 2004: ≈2.3 lakh dead in 14 countries, India ≈10,700 (Nagapattinam, A&N worst) + boats, harbours, fishing livelihoods lost + farmland salinised + tourism hit

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>NDMA guideline</b>
  <toggle>
  NDMA Tsunami 2010

  - Inundation and hazard maps + monitoring networks
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8162-ac94-df44ea6fe9fb/4251111b-206d-81cc-90cf-001cf05f53d6">Bio-shields</span> (mangroves, shelterbelts) + built barriers + safe coastal construction (CRZ)
  - Coastal drills + capacity building
  </toggle>
- <b>P</b>: mangrove bio-shields (Pichavaram reduced 2004 damage) + CRZ no-development zones
- <b>A</b>: regular coastal drills
- <b>E</b>: Indian Tsunami Early Warning System (INCOIS, Hyderabad, 2007): detects Indian Ocean quakes in under 10 minutes + last-mile alerts (SACHET)
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Floods

- Frame: 12% of land (40 million ha) flood-prone + 85% of the 1,200 mm rain falls in 3–4 months

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>P</b>: no city flood plan + 52% of towns have no master plan
- <b>N</b>: extreme rain, cyclones, snowmelt
- <b>C</b>: drains and wetlands encroached (Mumbai's Mithi river)
- <b>H</b>: concrete stops infiltration + deforestation, siltation + embankment breaches
- <b>F</b>: city own revenue only ≈1% of GDP

<b>Effects</b>: deaths, homes and crops lost + water-borne disease + transport and power cut

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>NDMA guideline</b>
  <toggle>
  NDMA Floods + Urban Floods 2010

  - Structural: reservoirs, embankments, desilting, catchment treatment
  - Non-structural: flood-plain zoning, flood forecasting, community preparedness (Aapda Mitra)
  - Urban Flood Guidelines 2010 + AMRUT stormwater drains + sponge-city ideas
  </toggle>
- <b>P</b>: flood-plain zoning + sponge cities
- <b>R</b>: Flood Hazard <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8135-b2ad-f873ca4bf49f/4251111b-206d-81c9-9fe6-001ce0630114">Atlas + Climate Smart Cities Assessment</span> Framework
- <b>E</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8121-af9f-ecad0aa50d46/4251111b-206d-81f6-acf9-001c6618b496">C-FLOOD f</span>orecasting
- <b>I</b>: devolve urban planning to ULBs (74th Amendment)
- Urban floods
  <toggle>
  Urban floods

  - Mumbai, 26 July 2005: ≈944 mm in 24 hours + Mithi river encroached + drains built for 25 mm/hour → ≈1,000 dead
  - Chennai, Dec 2015: extreme rain + sudden release from Chembarambakkam lake + lakes and Adyar floodplain built over → ≈340+ dead
  - Urban flood risk 3.6–7x by 2070 (World Bank) + urban people 480 million (2020) → 951 million (2050)
  </toggle>
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Landslides

- Frame: 12.6–15% of land (0.42 million sq km): Himalaya, Western Ghats, NE hills, Nilgiris

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>P</b>: building on steep slopes unregulated (Aizawl, Sikkim)
- <b>N</b>: intense rain + quakes + weak geology (Western Ghats: basalt + steep slopes)
- <b>C</b>: slopes levelled for farming (Malin 2014)
- <b>H</b>: road cutting, deforestation, mining, blasting, hydel projects

<b>Effects</b>: homes buried + roads, power, hydel cut + debris dams rivers → flash floods downstream

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>NDMA guideline</b>
  <toggle>
  NDMA Landslides + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81e1-96c9-ebe85e1012ec/4251111b-206d-8117-b12d-001c4d4d8a33">NLRMS 2019</span>

  - No construction on slopes of 30° or more + settlements and roads kept out of high-risk zones, farming in valleys
  - National Landslide Risk Management Strategy (2019): hazard mapping (GSI) + monitoring and early warning + awareness + capacity building + mountain zone rules + stabilisation (Landslide Risk Mitigation Scheme)
  - <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-817e-adf8-e1c1dc6a7138/4251111b-206d-817b-beb5-001cae454be4">Bhusanket portal</span> + landslide insurance
  </toggle>
- <b>P</b>: retaining walls, bunds, terrace farming, afforestation
- <b>R</b>: hazard zonation mapping
  <toggle>
  Zonation mapping

  - Divide hill terrain into zones by how likely landslides are
  - Inputs: slope + geology + soil + drainage + land use + rainfall + past landslides; made with GIS, satellites, field checks
  - Scales: 1:50,000 (GSI national) → 1:10,000 (town planning) → site level
  - Use: where not to build + road and dam alignment + where to put early warning sensors
  </toggle>
- <b>E</b>: slope sensors + rain-threshold warnings
- Related
  <toggle>
  Land subsidence

  - Ground sinks as soil or rock below is compressed: groundwater pumping + mining + building
  - Delhi worst (51 mm a year, 2,000+ buildings at risk) + Joshimath, Mussoorie
  - Fix<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8123-96c7-d531fcd8f97f/4251111b-206d-81ad-af9e-001c9b06d367">: aquifer recharge + InSAR satellite monitoring</span>
  </toggle>
- Cases: Wayanad, 30 July 2024 (200+ dead) · Malin, Pune 2014 (≈150, slopes levelled for farming) · Joshimath 2023
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Cloudburst

- Frame: ≥10 cm of rain in an hour over ≈20–30 sq km

<toggle>
Mechanism

- <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8152-b8eb-e97aac0faf28/4251111b-206d-81ae-b13c-001ca0272678">Orographic lift</span> pushes warm, moist air up the Himalay<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8152-b8eb-e97aac0faf28/4251111b-206d-8140-94e3-001c2201b39c">a → tall cumulonimbus clouds</span>
- Constant moisture inflow, the cloud can't release it gradually → sudden, localised downpour → flash floods
- Warming: air holds more moisture → shorter, more intense bursts
</toggle>

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>I</b>: hard to forecast, no local warning (Dharali 2025)
- <b>N</b>: orographic lift + stalled convective systems
- <b>C</b>: pilgrim and tourist crowds in risky valleys (Kedarnath 2013)
- <b>H</b>: settlements, roads and hydel projects in narrow valleys

<b>Effects</b>: flash floods + debris flows + roads, bridges, hydel projects washed away + pilgrims trapped

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>NDMA guideline</b>
  <toggle>
  NDMA Cloudburst

  - Settle on hard rock or firm ground + regulate construction
  - Control water infiltration + surface and sub-surface drainage
  - Bioengineering with local vegetation to hold slopes
  </toggle>
- <b>P</b>: amend building by-laws for risk-sensitive planning + better storm-water drainage
- <b>R</b>: landslide hazard zonation
- <b>F</b>: multi-hazard insurance
- <b>E</b>: last-mile warnings
- <b>I</b>: Centre–state coordination on rules and standards
- Cases: Kedarnath 2013 · Mandi, Himachal 2025 · Chasoti, Kishtwar, Aug 2025 (≈65 dead on the Machail yatra route)
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Cyclone

- Frame: India faces ≈10% of the world's tropical cyclones

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>N</b>: sea above ≈26.5°<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81ef-b65c-f76ff007113f/4251111b-206d-814f-b2e2-001caf6ada13">C + Coriolis force</span> + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81ef-b65c-f76ff007113f/4251111b-206d-8112-9fce-001cde38bdbe">low wind shear ·</span> warming → more Category 4–5 storms (IPCC AR6)
- <b>H</b>: mangroves cleared

<b>Effects</b>: storm surge, winds, floods + farmland salinised + coastal erosion + ports and power hit

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>NDMA guideline</b>
  <toggle>
  NDMA Cyclone 2008

  - IMD satellites + Doppler radars + four-colour warning code (green to red)
  - Cyclone shelters + roads + mangrove bio-shields
  - National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project: 13 cyclone-prone states and UTs (World Bank-supported)
  </toggle>
- <b>P</b>: multipurpose shelters + cyclone-resilient housing + mangrove bio-shields
- <b>R</b>: Odisha's zero-casualty model everywhere (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81b7-bfaa-dd2748f90ed4/4251111b-206d-81b1-862f-001cdc31718e">OSDMA,</span> first state DM authority, 1999)
- <b>E</b>: IMD four-colour warnings to the last mile
- Cases: Phailin 2013 (≈44 deaths vs ≈10,000 in 1999) · Fani 2019 (≈12 lakh evacuated) · recent: Dana, Fengal, Remal (2024), Montha, Ditwah (2025)
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Drought

- Frame: rainfall deficiency of 26% or more + 68% of land drought-prone

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>P</b>: poor water management (Cherrapunji paradox: wettest place, dry in winter)
- <b>N</b>: rainfall deficit + El Niño
- <b>H</b>: groundwater over-extraction + deforestation

<b>Effects</b>: crop failure, debt + drinking water and fodder shortage + distress migration

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>NDMA guideline</b>
  <toggle>
  NDMA Drought 2010

  - State Drought Monitoring Cells + real-time vulnerability maps + ICT control rooms
  - Watershed development + automatic weather stations + short-duration seeds + fodder banks
  - Drought insurance + market support + capacity building of PRIs and ULBs
  - Approach: reactive (relief) → proactive (early warning, stocks) → prospective (climate-smart farming)
  </toggle>
- <b>P</b>: watershed development (<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8152-bf4c-fc1563a7ada0/4251111b-206d-812a-aeca-001c979cd744">DPAP since</span> 1973–74)
- <b>R</b>: real-time vulnerability maps (State Drought Monitoring Cells)
- <b>F</b>: drought insurance
- <b>E</b>: El Niño and La Niña forecasts
- Cases: Marathwada 2015–16 (Latur got water by train) · 2002 (monsoon ≈19% short, El Niño year) · Rayalaseema, Andhra 2024
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Heatwaves

- Frame: IMD: plains ≥40°C and ≥4.5°C above normal (severe >6.4°C), or ≥45°C (severe ≥47°C) · 57% of districts (≈75% of people) at high heat risk (CEEW)

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>N</b>: anticyclones + clear skies + El Niño + hot westerlies · warm nights rising faster than warm days
- <b>H</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81a9-8a30-ff045dcdb96c/4251111b-206d-819a-855e-001c0fbdee85">urban heat island +</span> rising humidity (north India 30–40% → 40–50%)

<b>Effects</b>: ≈10,000 dead (2000–2020) + work capacity down up to 40% + crop losses + power demand spikes

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>NDMA guideline</b>
  <toggle>
  NDMA Heat Action Plans

  - Heat Action Plans: expand from ≈300 cities to 4,800 ULBs + turn them into fundable projects + plan for warm nights
  - Model: Ahmedabad HAP 2013, first in South Asia
  - National HAP Repository
  </toggle>
- <b>R</b>: IMD heat index
- <b>F</b>: heatwaves now a notified disaster (16th FC) → full SDRF use + parametric insurance
- <b>E</b>: IMD colour-coded warnings
- Cases: Andhra + Telangana 2015 (≈2,000+ dead) · North India 2024 (Churu 50.5°C)
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Lightning

- Frame: Mar–Apr 2025: 160+ dead in 12 states, up 184% on 2024 (Bihar, UP worst)
- Causes: <b>N</b> pre-monsoon heat + moisture → tall cumulonimbus clouds, more as the climate warms
- Effects: deaths mostly of farmers in open fields + livestock lost
- Solutions: <b>E</b> Damini app (20–40 km, 40 minutes ahead) + forecasts 5 days to 3 hours ahead · <b>F</b> notified disaster (16th FC) → SDRF for arresters and shelters · <b>A</b> awareness in Bihar, UP villages + Lightning Action Plans
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Wildfires

- Frame: 36% of forest cover fire-prone (4% extremely, 6% very highly)
- Causes: <b>N</b> drought, heat, wind, lightning + lantana and pine litter · <b>C</b> field burning, campfires, shifting cultivation
- Effects: biodiversity and carbon sink lost + smoke + soil erosion + forest livelihoods hit

<toggle>
<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81cb-8b5e-c3a16f3949ec/4251111b-206d-81c7-9fb9-001c58e03c48">NAPFF 2018</span>

- National Action Plan on Forest Fires (2018) + Forest Fire Prevention & Management Scheme (community participation)
- FSI pre-warning alerts + Large Forest Fire Monitoring <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-811c-8619-e67b820bdd27/4251111b-206d-81fa-a7a8-001c56d55085">(SNPP-VIIRS</span> satellite) + burnt-area maps (AWiFS)
</toggle>

- Solutions: <b>P</b> firebreaks + clear lantana and pine litter · <b>A</b> community fire watchers · <b>E</b> alerts to the last village
- Case: Uttarakhand 2024
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Himalayan hazards (GLOF + Sturzstrom)

- Frame: GLOF = sudden release of water held by a <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81d1-906f-dc0e272823d0/4251111b-206d-81d0-8406-001c823076e2">glacier or moraine dam</span> · since 1990 glacial lake number / area / volume up 53% / 51% / 48% · 7,500 lakes above 4,500 m

<toggle>
Sturzstrom

- Huge rock-ice collapse that travels very far: friction melts ice → water lubricates the base → debris flow within minutes
- Chamoli 2021: ≈25 million m³ of rock and ice = rock-ice avalanche, not a moraine-dam GLOF (South Lhonak 2023 was)
- Warning gap: minutes of lead time → needs SAR/InSAR, permafrost mapping, local sirens
</toggle>

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>N</b>: glacier melt + moraine or ice dam failure + quakes + permafrost thaw
- <b>H</b>: hydropower, roads, tourism (≈100 million tourists a year in the Himalaya)

<b>Effects</b>: >9 million at risk in High Mountain Asia + villages, roads and hydel dams wiped out (Chungthang 2023)

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>NDMA guideline</b>
  <toggle>
  NDMA GLOF 2020

  - Lower risky lakes: siphoning, controlled breaching, outlet structures + embankments
  - Early warning at 56 at-risk lake<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81e7-afd1-ff25066febb1/4251111b-206d-81b5-899c-001cfe9d8290">s + NRSC 24x7</span> lake watch
  - National GLOF Risk Mitigation Project: HP, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal
  </toggle>
- <b>P</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81b2-a7e6-d8628404af42/4251111b-206d-814f-a4a1-001cb5c92b78">CEA slope-stability guidelines</span> for hydro projects
- <b>R</b><span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81ab-b768-cd3eb3cc7c8d/4251111b-206d-8113-832b-001cf6baba28">: CWC monitors</span> 900+ lakes + risk indexing
- <b>I</b>: <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81f5-9187-fe7abcaa3b0f/4251111b-206d-819b-bd6a-001c8adf726e">ICIMOD c</span>ooperation across the Hindu Kush Himalaya
- Cases: South Lhonak, Sikkim 2023 · Chamoli 2021 · Kedarnath 2013
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Dams

- Frame: India is the 3rd largest dam owner: 6,628 specified dams (Maharashtra most)

<b>Causes of failure</b>

- <b>N</b>: floods beyond design (overtopping) + quakes (Bhuj 2001) + GLOFs (Chungthang 2023)
- <b>H</b>: ageing: 80% over 25 years, ≈26% over 50 + silt has cut storage ≈19% + poor maintenance and monitoring

<b>Effects</b>: sudden flood wave downstream → deaths, towns wiped out + farmland, power and water supply lost

<b>Solutions</b>

- <b>P</b>: IoT sensors + drones and <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-813f-9f09-f8b3197ec3f9/4251111b-206d-815d-b7c2-001c23cbbd9f">underwater ROVs</span> for inspection + sediment bypass (Japan) + lifecycle management
- <b>I</b>: Dam Safety Act 2021 (4-tier institutions = inter-agency)
  <toggle>
  Dam Safety Act 2021

  - 4-tier institutions at Centre and states for surveillance, inspection, maintenance
  - DRIP (rehabilitation<span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-81fd-9041-e17260b25bce/4251111b-206d-8140-bf88-001c1542746b">) + DHARMA app</span> + National Register of Large Dams + National Centre for Earthquake Safety of Dams (MNIT Jaipur)
  </toggle>
- Cases
  <toggle>
  Dam failures

  - Machchhu dam, Morbi, Gujarat (1979)
  - Banqiao, China (1975) · Derna, Libya (2023)
  </toggle>
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Human-made disasters

<b>Causes</b>

- <b>P</b>: weak enforcement (Factories Act 1948; Vizag LG Polymers ran without valid clearance) + National Building Code only advisory
- <b>I</b>: little crowd-density tech + old equipment
- <b>C</b>: rules ignored + panic and rumours (79% of stampedes at religious events)
- <b>H</b>: human error + poor maintenance + overcrowding + too few fire stations (5,191 in 2019)
- <b>F</b>: little investment in safety
- <b>C</b>: organisers and police don't coordinate (Chinnaswamy, Bengaluru 2025)

<toggle>
Industrial accidents

- ≈1,861 <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8178-ba7e-cc1f61c7dbb8/4251111b-206d-8191-885a-001c22002423">Major Accident Hazard sites</span>
- Bhopal 1984 (methyl isocyanate, ≈5 lakh affected) · Vizag LG Polymers 2020 (styrene, 12 dead, no valid clearance, NGT ₹50 crore)
- Law: absolute liability (MC Mehta, Oleum gas 1986) + EPA 1986 + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-812a-b856-f53dd043ad6c/4251111b-206d-8196-b509-001c8bba19bd">MSIHC Rules 1989 + Public Liability Insurance Act 1991</span> + NDMA Chemical Disaster Guidelines 2007
</toggle>

<toggle>
Fire safety

- 5,888 deaths in 2024 (NCRB) · causes: non-compliance (coaching centres, hospitals, Rajkot gaming zone)
- Fire services = State subject <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-815e-a940-c09c910266eb/4251111b-206d-814e-8e47-001c64387841">(Art 243W, 12th Schedule)</span> + National Building Code only advisory + staff shortage
- Fix (NDMA): State Fire Act + third-party fire audits before NOCs + district fire chiefs
</toggle>

Stampedes

- NDMA crowd guide 2014: capacity planning + risk analysis + <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-818a-9af2-f40ae5bdcc5f/4251111b-206d-818d-891b-001c964a0bcf">failure-mode analysis</span>
- <span discussion-urls="discussion://4221111b-206d-80b0-a97f-e118421fe6d8/4251111b-206d-8126-a0aa-d3a0b44f90e8/4251111b-206d-8162-8b91-001cd686377a">FIST model (Fruin)</span>: Force, Information, Space, Time
- Tech: RFID (Kumbh, Vaishno Devi) + AI CCTV and drones (Hajj)

<toggle>
OLD way

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Seismic and Disaster Statistics

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: <span color="green_bg">59% landmass</span> prone to moderate to very high intensity earthquakes
  - According to IDMC, 13–23 million people are displaced globally each year due to disasters; in 2024, India alone saw 5.4 million internal displacements, 40 million hectares susceptible to flood and river erosion 5700 out of 7500 coastline risk of cyclones and tsunamis 68% of cultivable area
- <b>Significance</b>: India is multi-hazard prone → <span color="green_bg">DRR</span> has to be part of all development planning
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 India’s Disaster Approach

<toggle color="gray">
PYQ 2020

- <b>2020 Q18 (15 marks):</b> Discuss the recent measures initiated in disaster management by the Government of India departing from the earlier reactive approach.
</toggle>

- India’s approach : from Relief centric approach to a <span color="green_bg">zero casualty</span> approach and National Disaster plan management india (make india disaster resilient in all sectors ) (<span color="green_bg">NDMP 2019</span> focuses on six thematic areas: Understanding Risk, Inter-Agency Coordination, Disaster Risk Governance, Capacity Development, Preparedness and Response, Recovery and Rehabilitation.
- <b>Examples</b>: Odisha, Cyclone Phailin 2013 (worked: \~10 lakh evacuated, \~44 deaths vs \~10,000 in the 1999 super cyclone → <span color="green_bg">zero-casualty approach</span>) + Kerala floods 2018 (failed: dam releases poorly coordinated, \~480 dead)
- <b>DRR + climate adaptation</b>: same goal = less risk → <span color="green_bg">Sendai + Paris + SDGs</span> (all 2015) to be read together → India: NDMP 2019 aligns all three + climate-proof infrastructure via <span color="green_bg">CDRI</span>
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Disaster Risk Formula

<toggle color="gray">
PYQ 2019, 2013

- <b>2019 Q8 (10 marks):</b> Vulnerability is an essential element for defining disaster impacts and its threat to people. How and in what ways can vulnerability to disasters be characterized? Discuss different types of vulnerability with reference to disasters.
- <b>2013 Q18 (10 marks):</b> How important are vulnerability and risk assessment for pre-disaster management? As an administrator, what are key areas that you would focus on in a Disaster Management System?
</toggle>

- Disaster Risk = <span color="green_bg">Hazard × Vulnerability</span> × Exposure (triad is foundation of Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Hazard Zoning and Risk Mapping, <span color="green_bg">Early Warning</span> Systems, Resilient Development Planning) (eg;. In Sikkim, the 2023 Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) from South Lhonak Lake caused major destruction downstream. The hazard (GLOF) became a high disaster risk due to vulnerable infrastructure, exposed settlements, and lack of <span color="green_bg">early warning</span>.)
- Vulnerability = how likely people or assets are to be harmed + how little they can cope → 4 types: physical (weak houses on unsafe slopes) + social (age, gender, caste, disability, literacy) + economic (poverty, informal jobs, no insurance) + environmental (degraded ecosystems, deforestation)
- Eg: Himachal flash floods 2023 (Mandi, Kullu, Shimla): building on unstable slopes = physical + environmental vulnerability
- Exposure = people and assets sitting in the hazard zone (high exposure → damage even if vulnerability is low)
- <b>Hazard vs disaster vs risk</b>: hazard = an event that can cause harm (cyclone) → disaster = when it overwhelms a community's <span color="green_bg">capacity to cope</span> → risk = chance of loss = hazard × vulnerability × exposure (lower with more capacity)
- <b>Cascading / compound risk</b>: one hazard sets off another → Chamoli 2021 (rock-ice avalanche → flood → Tapovan tunnel) + Sikkim 2023 (GLOF → Chungthang dam breach) + Japan 2011 (quake → tsunami → Fukushima) → plan for <span color="green_bg">chains of hazards</span>, not single ones (Sendai)
- <b>Examples</b>: Joshimath 2023 (town on old landslide debris = high exposure + vulnerability → sinking)
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Insurance Coverage

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: Only 1% of india insurance protection
- <b>Significance</b>: faster recovery + less load on SDRF/NDRF
- <b>Examples</b>: Nagaland (2024, worked: first state to buy <span color="green_bg">parametric insurance</span> → automatic payout when rain crosses a threshold) + PMFBY (mixed: claims paid late → Gujarat, Andhra and others left the scheme in 2020)
- <b>India's response</b>: Insurance GST reduced to 0 % to enhance coverage + Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India’s (IRDAI) overarching vision of achieving "<span color="green_bg">Insurance for All by 2047</span>." + The Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act (Dec 2025) + PM FASAL BIMA YOJANA
- <b>Challenges</b>: <span color="green_bg">protection gap</span>: most disaster losses uninsured + low awareness + late claims
- <b>Way forward</b>: parametric cover for states and cities + risk pooling + insurance bundled with schemes
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Examples of Disaster Innovation

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: new tech and local ideas used to warn, coordinate and teach in disasters
- <b>Examples</b>: During <span color="green_bg">Cyclone Hudhud</span>, Visakhapatnam’s PWD used WhatsApp groups for resource tracking and team coordination + Disaster detection: E.g. Earthquake detection through X (Formerly twitter), COVID 19 Chatbots by WHO
- <b>India's response</b>: Disaster awareness is now part of the NCERT curriculum in Classes 8 to 10, The IUINDRR-NIDM network, with over 330+ universities, promotes disaster risk research. E.g., building hazard maps using AI, Odisha State Disaster Mitigation Authority has developed a web based platform called “SATARK” to provide warning information for various hazards
- <b>Challenges</b>: digital divide + fake news on social media in disasters
- <b>Way forward</b>: <span color="green_bg">Common Alerting Protocol</span> (SACHET) + cell-broadcast alerts + AI hazard maps for every district
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Disaster Management Cycle

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: Phases: before (prevention, mitigation → preparedness) → during (response) → after (recovery = rehabilitation + reconstruction) → <span color="green_bg">build back better</span> feeds the next round of prevention
- <b>Significance</b>: moves focus from relief after the event to <span color="green_bg">risk reduction</span> before it
- <b>Examples</b>: Odisha after the 1999 super cyclone (worked: OSDMA set up 1999 → shelters, drills, warnings → Phailin 2013, Fani 2019 with few deaths = full cycle working) + Uttarakhand 2013 (failed: no preparedness or warning → Kedarnath, 5,000+ dead or missing)
- <b>India's response</b>: DM Act 2005 moved India from <span color="green_bg">relief-centric</span> to the whole cycle + <span color="green_bg">NDMP 2019</span> gives each phase to nodal ministries
- <b>Challenges</b>: many states still relief-heavy + mitigation money under-used
- <b>Way forward</b>: DRR in every phase + build back better as the rule, not the exception
- Disaster management cycle :

<image source="notion-file-block://4221111b-206d-800d-beb6-dfa1ab7fbdab/3eead246-26af-4ca3-802b-c17c6267c798?space_id=3939cd2d-3e25-404f-9196-d463e4c2e65e&name=RISK_MANAGEMENT.png" />
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Components of Prevention

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: steps that stop a hazard becoming a disaster or cut its impact before it strikes
- <b>Pillars / key features</b>: Components of prevention : 1) Hazard mapping and risk zoning (e.g., seismic zoning maps), <span color="green_bg">Retrofitting</span> of buildings and infrastructure, Flood embankments, cyclone shelters, <span color="green_bg">early warning</span> system, Policy and regulation (e.g., land-use planning, building codes, coastal regulation zones), Environmental conservation (e.g., afforestation, wetland protection)
- <b>Significance</b>: every \$1 on mitigation saves about \$6 in losses (US NIBS 2019)
- <b>Examples</b>: Odisha's multipurpose cyclone shelters (worked) + Joshimath 2023 (failed: the Mishra Committee warned against heavy construction back in 1976 → ignored)
- <b>India's response</b>: BIS codes + National Building Code + <span color="green_bg">hazard zonation</span> maps + <span color="green_bg">mitigation funds</span> (NDMF / SDMF from the 15th FC)
- <b>Challenges</b>: building codes poorly enforced + expert warnings ignored (Joshimath)
- <b>Way forward</b>: risk-informed land use + retrofit schools and hospitals first
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Components of Preparedness

- Components of prepardness : Development of disaster management plans (national, state, district levels)
- Training of first responders (e.g., <span color="green_bg">Aapda Mitra</span> volunteers, civil defence, police), Conducting mock drills, simulations, and community awareness campaigns, Stockpiling emergency supplies and equipment, Development of <span color="green_bg">early warning</span> systems and communication protocols (e.g., CAP-SACHET)
- <span color="green_bg">Mission Mausam</span> was approved by the Union Cabinet on September 11, 2024, with a budget of ₹2,000 crore over two years (2024–26), aimed at making India "Weather Ready and Climate Smart."
  - Key features: deployment of 50 Doppler Weather Radars, 60 Radio Sonde/Radio Wind stations, 100 disdrometers, 10 Wind Profilers, and 25 radiometers; integration of AI/ML with physics-based numerical models for improved forecasts.
  - "Mausam GPT" — an AI-powered system providing quick and reliable weather information in both text and audio forms — is being developed and will be rolled out over the next five years
- Bharat Forecast System (IITM Pune): forecast grid 12 km → 6 km, finer than US/UK/EU models + village-level nowcasts
- Exercise Suraksha Chakra (August 2025): the first integrated multi-state mock drill in Delhi-NCR, conducted across 55 locations covering 18 districts in Delhi, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh, simulating a large-scale earthquake. Organised by NDMA with the Indian Army, DDMA, and state SDMAs.
- The Hyper-Velocity EWS Challenge: Standard hydrological Early Warning Systems (EWS) are often rendered ineffective during sturzstrom and flash-debris events because travel velocity is extreme (minutes rather than hours), leaving negligible lead time.
  - DRR Priority: Requires high-altitude satellite monitoring (SAR/InSAR), permafrost thermal mapping, cross-border data sharing (transboundary early warning), and localized sirens rather than downstream-only gauge sensors.
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Components of Response

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: action during and just after a disaster to save lives and meet basic needs
- <b>Pillars / key features</b>: Components of response : Search and rescue operations by <span color="green_bg">NDRF</span>, SDRF, armed forces, Provision of emergency shelter, food, water, and medical aid, Restoration of critical infrastructure (power, roads, communication), Coordinated efforts by central and state agencies, NGOs, and community volunteers, Emergency health care and psychological support
- <b>Significance</b>: the <span color="green_bg">golden hour</span>: most lives are saved by fast local rescue
- <b>Examples</b>: Silkyara tunnel, Uttarakhand (2023, worked: 41 workers rescued after 17 days, multi-agency + rat-hole miners) + Kedarnath 2013 (failed: late warning + poor coordination)
- <b>India's response</b>: NDRF (16 battalions) + SDRF in every state + <span color="green_bg">Incident Response System</span> (NDMP) + ERSS-112 + armed forces for HADR
- <b>Challenges</b>: last-mile reach + coordination gaps between agencies
- <b>Way forward</b>: regular IRS drills + trained community first responders (<span color="green_bg">Aapda Mitra</span>)
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Components of Recovery

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: restoring lives, livelihoods and infrastructure after a disaster, ideally better than before
- <b>Pillars / key features</b>: Components of recovery : Damage assessment and compensation, Restoration of public services and livelihoods, Reconstruction of housing, schools, health centres, and other infrastructure, Integration of disaster risk reduction (DRR) and climate resilience into redevelopment, Psycho-social rehabilitation and community participation in rebuilding
- <b>Examples</b>: Bhuj 2001 → Gujarat (worked: GSDMA + <span color="green_bg">owner-driven reconstruction</span> + new building rules = <span color="green_bg">build back better</span>) + Kerala 2018 → Rebuild Kerala Initiative (mixed: slow spending)
- <b>India's response</b>: <span color="green_bg">PDNA</span> (post-disaster needs assessment) + Recovery & Reconstruction window in disaster funds (15th FC) + livelihood support via MGNREGA
- <b>Challenges</b>: slow release of funds + rebuilding in the same risky places
- <b>Way forward</b>: owner-driven, <span color="green_bg">risk-informed</span> rebuilding + PDNA after every major disaster
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Disaster Resilience

<toggle color="gray">
PYQ 2024

- <b>2024 Q17 (15 marks):</b> What is disaster resilience? How is it determined? Describe various elements of a resilience framework. Also mention the global targets of Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030).
</toggle>

- Disaster resilience : can <span color="green_bg">anticipate, absorb, adapt and recover</span> quickly
- Resilience = anticipate + absorb + adapt + recover, and "<span color="green_bg">bounce forward</span>" (build back better), not just bounce back
- Measured by: anticipate (early warning, risk information, education) + absorb (strong infrastructure, safety nets) + adapt (flexible institutions, risk-informed development) + recover (fast, inclusive rebuilding with community)
- Eg: coastal village with cyclone shelters + trained volunteers is more resilient than one without
- <b>Examples</b>: Odisha, Cyclone Fani 2019 (worked: \~12 lakh evacuated, \~64 deaths) + Chennai floods 2015 (failed: lakes and floodplains built over → city could not absorb the rain)
- <b>India's response</b>: <span color="green_bg">CDRI</span> (2019) + Aapda Mitra volunteers + Mission Mausam + resilient-infrastructure chapters in NDMP
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Accountability and Oversight

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: Supreme Court & High Courts have played a critical role in enforcing accountability (e.g.,
- Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana case, COVID migrant workers case), Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) and Parliamentary Committees have flagged issues in fund utilization, inter-agency coordination, and absence of mitigation plans.
- <b>Examples</b>: CAG audit of NDMA (2013: projects stalled, plans missing) + SC, <span color="green_bg">Gaurav Kumar Bansal</span> (2021: NDMA must set ex gratia for COVID deaths)
- <b>Challenges</b>: no fixed liability for officials + funds left unspent (CAG)
- <b>Way forward</b>: <span color="green_bg">social audits</span> of relief + DM plans with timelines + regular review of NDMA by Parliament
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Disaster Management Act, 2005

- Three-Tier Mechanism: Disaster management is structured at National (NDMA), State (SDMA), and District (DDMA) levels
- NDMA: Apex body chaired by PM; lays policies, approves plans, supervises <span color="green_bg">NDRF</span>, and oversees funds for mitigation and preparedness
- National Executive Committee (NEC): Chaired by Union Home Secretary; coordinates and monitors disaster management across ministries
- Statutory Disaster Plans: National, State, and District plans are mandatory and must align with <span color="green_bg">sustainable development</span> principles
- NDRF: Specialized response force with trained battalions, engineers, paramedics, and dog squads; pre-positioned in threatening disaster situations
- Local Authorities: Panchayat, municipalities, and ULBs play legally defined roles in preparedness, relief, and reconstruction. Fund via NDRF (fund) (used for rehab) and SDRF (only for immediate mitigation) and The National Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF), created by the 11th Finance Commission, was later merged with the NDRF.
- Recommendations of the Standing Committee on Finance (2019)(Chairperson: Dr. M. Veerappa Moily)
  - Relief scale: Increase SDRF/NDRF aid, including infrastructure restoration
  - Mitigation fund: Create a separate fund for permanent disaster mitigation projects
  - Funding issues: NCCD revenue declining; 10% of central scheme funds should restore damaged assets
  - SDRF corpus: Raise annual allocation from 5% to 15% (2020–2025) to meet state needs
- <b>Examples</b>: COVID-19 (Mar 2020, worked as a tool: first nationwide use of the Act for lockdown orders) + Uttarakhand 2013 (failed: CAG found the state authority had barely met before Kedarnath)
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 Disaster Management Amendment Act 2025

<toggle color="gray">
PYQ 2020

- <b>2020 Q18 (15 marks):</b> Discuss the recent measures initiated in disaster management by the Government of India departing from the earlier reactive approach.
</toggle>

<ul>
<li>
Expands definitions of disaster risk, resilience, recovery aligns with global frameworks (SFDRR) and strengthens disaster governance
</li>
<li>
<span color="green_bg">Urban DM Authorities</span>: All Municipal Corporations (except Delhi & Chandigarh) must have Urban DM Authorities headed by Municipal Commissioners
</li>
<li>
National & State Disaster Databases: Mandates real-time databases for risk, response, mitigation, damage, and relief — essential for planning and audits
</li>
<li>
Enhanced NDMA & SDRFs: NDMA can monitor plans, set minimum relief standards, audit implementations; all states must have SDRFs mirroring <span color="green_bg">NDRF</span> but some issues remain like no upgradation is status of NDMA (still under MHA), doesn’t address member vacancy, fund thru MHA, vague details on urban DM plans, weak linkage with tech.
</li>
<li>
<b>Localisation of DRR (₹507 cr panchayat project)</b> 

- <span color="green_bg">Community-based DRR</span>: locals identify, plan and act on their own risks (Sendai asks for it) + communities are the first responders
- National Project for Community-Based DRR in PRIs (₹507.37 cr; MoPR + NDMA): 20 states, 81 disaster-prone districts, 20 GPs per district + 1 Model Gram Panchayat per state on 6 hazard themes
- Local examples: Pozhuthana panchayat (Kerala floods 2018: risk maps, village response teams, EOC) + Tampara wetland (Odisha, eco-DRR)
- Tools: Aapda Mitra + eGramSwaraj, Gram Manchitra + SACHET alerts
</li>
</ul>
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Legal Framework for Disasters

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: <span color="green_bg">DM Act, 2005</span> = main law (NDMA → SDMA → DDMA) + sector laws below
- <b>Pillars / key features</b>: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 Addresses chemical and ecological disasters
- Factories Act, 1948 Worker safety and industrial disaster prevention
- The <span color="green_bg">Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897</span> Legal framework for biological disasters (e.g., COVID-19)
- Atomic Energy Act, 1962 For radiological and nuclear emergencies
- The Water Act, 1974 & Air Act, 1981 Prevent pollution-induced disasters
- Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 Prevents ecological degradation leading to disasters
- National green tribunal : Strengthen enforcement of environmental laws like Air Act, Water Act, Environment Protection Act.
- <b>Examples</b>: COVID-19, 2020 (DM Act + Epidemic Diseases Act used together for lockdowns) + Bhopal 1984 → EPA 1986 + Public Liability Insurance Act 1991
- <b>India's response</b>: DM (Amendment) Act, 2025: urban DM authorities + national and state disaster databases
- <b>Challenges</b>: laws scattered across ministries + weak liability for chemical disasters
- <b>Way forward</b>: one risk-based approach across laws + enforce the 2025 amendments
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) 2019

<toggle color="gray">
PYQ 2018

- <b>2018 Q18 (15 marks):</b> Describe various measures taken in India for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) before and after signing ‘Sendai Framework for DRR (2015-2030)’. How is this framework different from ‘Hyogo Framework for Action, 2005’?
</toggle>

- The National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) 2019 updates India’s first plan (2016) and aligns with SFDRR, SDGs, <span color="green_bg">Paris Agreement</span>, and India’s Ten-Point DRR Agenda. It provides a comprehensive framework for prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery, and “<span color="green_bg">build back better</span>.”
- Thematic areas include risk assessment, inter-agency coordination, structural and non-structural DRR investments, capacity development, and climate risk management, with special focus on vulnerable groups and mainstreaming DRR into development.
- <span color="green_bg">NDMP 2019</span> sets short-, medium-, and long-term objectives (2022, 2027, 2030) and includes hazard-specific risk matrices for 20+ natural and anthropogenic disasters.
- The response framework defines roles of nodal ministries, Incident Response Teams, early warning systems, and central support to state governments. Capacity building involves PRIs, ULBs, communities, professionals, educational institutions, civil society, and private sector to ensure decentralized, inclusive disaster governance.
- <b>Examples</b>: Ahmedabad <span color="green_bg">Heat Action Plan</span> (2013, first in South Asia → model for heat chapters) + Cyclone Fani 2019 (SOPs, NDRF pre-positioned, IMD warnings in sync)
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
⚪ SDG 13.1.2

- Tracks the number of countries adopting and implementing national disaster risk reduction strategies aligned with the Sendai Framework (2015–2030).
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟡 Early Warning Systems

- <b>Definition & India's status</b>: systems that detect a hazard and warn people in time to act
- <b>Significance</b>: The Pacific Rim Tsunami Warning system is an example of a cost-effective warning system; its yearly operating cost is approximately US\$4 million. The yearly operating cost of a hypothetical global warning system is estimated at US\$30 million. This cost, compared to the international aid donations of nearly US\$8 billion for the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami, clearly demonstrates the cost effectiveness of such a system.
- <b>Examples</b>: INCOIS tsunami warning centre, Hyderabad (2007, worked: alerts within minutes, serves the Indian Ocean) + Dharali, Uttarkashi (Aug 2025, failed: flash flood in a narrow valley with no local warning)
- <b>India's response</b>: <span color="green_bg">SACHET</span> <span color="green_bg">Common Alerting Protocol</span> + Mission Mausam + Bharat Forecast System + Damini (lightning) + cell-broadcast alert tests
- <b>Challenges</b>: <span color="green_bg">last-mile</span> gaps (Dharali) + cloudbursts and flash floods hard to forecast
- <b>Way forward</b>: UN Early Warnings for All (by 2027) + village sirens + alerts in local languages
</toggle>

<toggle heading="h4">
🟢 World Conferences on Disaster Risk Reduction (WCDRR)

<toggle color="gray">
PYQ 2024, 2018

- <b>2024 Q17 (15 marks):</b> What is disaster resilience? How is it determined? Describe various elements of a resilience framework. Also mention the global targets of Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030).
- <b>2018 Q18 (15 marks):</b> Describe various measures taken in India for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) before and after signing ‘Sendai Framework for DRR (2015-2030)’. How is this framework different from ‘Hyogo Framework for Action, 2005’?
</toggle>

- First WCDRR – Yokohama, Japan (1994)
  - Main Outcome: Yokohama Strategy and Plan of Action for a Safer World
  - Aims: Establish a global framework for disaster risk reduction (DRR). Promote disaster prevention, preparedness, and mitigation. Encourage international cooperation and support for DRR initiatives.
  - Key Features: Introduced the concept of disaster risk reduction as a global priority. Emphasized the importance of integrating DRR into development planning.
- Second WCDRR – Kobe, Japan (2005)
  - Main Outcome: <span color="green_bg">Hyogo Framework</span> for Action (HFA) 2005–2015
  - Aims: Build the resilience of nations and communities to disasters. Achieve a substantial reduction of disaster losses in lives and in the social, economic, and environmental assets of communities and countries.
  - Key Features: Outlined five priorities for action: 1. Making DRR a priority, 2. Improving risk information and <span color="green_bg">early warning</span>, 3. Building a culture of safety and resilience, 4. Reducing the risks in key sectors, 5. Strengthening preparedness for response.
  - Emphasized the need for a systematic approach to DRR.
  - Highlighted the importance of integrating DRR into development policies and planning
- Third WCDRR – Sendai, Japan (2015)
  - Main Outcome: <span color="green_bg">Sendai Framework</span> for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030
  - Aims: Achieve the substantial reduction of disaster risk and losses in lives, livelihoods, and health, and in the economic, physical, social, cultural, and environmental assets of persons, businesses, communities, and countries.
  - 4 reduce (by 2030): disaster deaths + people affected + economic loss (as % of GDP) + damage to critical infrastructure and basic services
  - 3 increase: countries with national and local DRR strategies (by 2020) + international support to developing countries + access to multi-hazard early warning and risk information
  - 4 priorities: understand risk + strengthen risk governance + invest in DRR for resilience + preparedness and build back better
  - India aligned via: NDMP 2016/2019 built on the 4 priorities + PM's 10-point agenda (2016) + CDRI (2019)
